Picture: Askeladden paddles his big old wooden kneading trough across the glassy fjord in the pale morning, the seven silver ducks crowded into the trough around him. Behind him, the stone door in the Dark Mountain stands ajar, and the Troll leans out of it, bellowing.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Askeladden: A lanky young man of about nineteen with messy straw-blond hair, sharp blue-grey eyes, a narrow freckled face and a calm, crooked smile. He wears a faded red knitted beanie, a navy work jacket over a grey T-shirt, black work trousers and scuffed white trainers.
- the Troll: An enormous, ancient fjord troll three times as tall as a man, with grey-green skin like weathered rock patched with moss and lichen, a long knobbly nose, tiny black eyes under bushy brows, a wide mouth with two stubby teeth, huge ears, a beard like dry grass and a small spruce growing from the top of his head. Setting:
- the Dark Mountain: A dark, steep mountain rising straight out of the far side of a narrow fjord, its lower slopes covered in black spruce, with a narrow pebble beach at its foot and a heavy, door-shaped slab of stone set into the rock face just above the waterline.

Story world: Present-day western Norway. The royal estate is a big, old white wooden manor with a glassed-in terrace, a lawn running down to a private quay, a boathouse and staff buildings, on one side of a narrow fjord. Straight across the fjord rises the Dark Mountain, where the troll lives behind a heavy stone door that grinds open in the rock. The seven silver ducks are real ducks of solid, gleaming silver, like small sculptures. The kneading trough is a big, old, dark wooden trough almost as long as a rowing boat; Askeladden paddles it with a worn wooden oar from the boathouse. The bedspread is a heavy quilt of alternating silver and gold squares. The golden harp is a small golden lap harp. Inside the mountain, ancient cave meets forgotten basement: raw concrete, metal shelving, old weights and a stone feasting hall.

This story's season, light and colours: Early summer on a western fjord: pale, cool mornings, glassy blue-green water, bright silver glints and white midsummer nights. Inside the mountain: flat fluorescent light on grey concrete, and warm lamp light in the stone hall.

Art style: Contemporary Scandinavian editorial illustration: flat, graphic shapes with subtle risograph grain and a little hand-drawn texture, clean confident lines and a limited palette of spot inks led by deep petrol blue, with fjord teal, lingonberry red, honey mustard, sage green, warm paper off-white and ink charcoal, like the pages of a risograph-printed book, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, in the cool, clear Nordic light of today. Present-day Norway: fjord towns, suburbs, farms with tractors, cabins, ferries, roadside petrol stations, offices and flats, grey rain and bright snow, with people in modern clothes such as rain jackets, knitted sweaters, hoodies, suits and work wear. The magic of the tale appears plainly in this everyday world: trolls, talking animals and enchantments look real and slightly absurd, drawn in the same flat style. Characters

Askeladden askeladden · Askeladden

Den yngste broren, en rolig og hardtarbeidende kjøkkenhjelp som bærer et gammelt knadetrau og vinner med kløkt framfor styrke.

A lanky young man of about nineteen with messy straw-blond hair, sharp blue-grey eyes, a narrow freckled face and a calm, crooked smile. He wears a faded red knitted beanie, a navy work jacket over a grey T-shirt, black work trousers and scuffed white trainers.

Kongen kongen · the King

En jordnær, kravstor konge som fortsatt bruker kongsgården når han ikke er i hovedstaden, og som lokkes av trollets skatter.

A stout, elderly king with a neat white beard, round tortoiseshell glasses, rosy cheeks and thinning white hair, a man used to getting his way. At home he wears a thick cream cardigan over a pale-blue shirt, brown corduroy trousers and sheepskin slippers.

Trollet ved fjellet trollet · the Troll

Et gammelt fjordtroll som bor i et mørkt fjell og vokter sølvender, et rutete sengeteppe av sølv og gull, og en gullharpe med humørmagi.

An enormous, ancient fjord troll three times as tall as a man, with grey-green skin like weathered rock patched with moss and lichen, a long knobbly nose, tiny black eyes under bushy brows, a wide mouth with two stubby teeth, huge ears, a beard like dry grass and a small spruce growing from the top of his head. He wears a huge, ragged, faded canvas work coat tied with rope, and goes barefoot on enormous flat feet.

Trolldatteren trolldatteren · the Troll's Daughter

Trollets datter som holder Askeladden fanget, tester om han er 'feit nok', og lar seg lure av hans rolige manipulasjon.

A huge troll woman, about three times as tall as a man, with a broad moss-green face, a long bumpy nose, small squinting eyes, heavy arms and one enormous, heavy red braid that reaches her knees. She wears an enormous faded grey hoodie, black leggings and a big knitted shawl, and goes barefoot.

Prinsessa prinsessa · the Princess

Kongens datter, en moderne prinsesse som blir lovet bort som belønning når Askeladden henter gullharpa.

A young woman in her early twenties with a sharp, curious face, dark hair in a short bob, brown eyes and a small gold stud in one ear. She wears a camel wool coat over a black turtleneck, dark jeans and ankle boots.

#05 · askeladden
modern · after paragraph 30
Til slutt skrapte det i stein, og en tung steindør gled på gløtt. En grå hånd, stor som et bildekk, hengte sengeteppet ut i sprekken til lufting. Det glitret i sølv og gull når vinden tok i det. Troll trengte visst også frisk luft i sengetøyet.

En grå hånd, stor som et bildekk, hengte sengeteppet ut til lufting.

Alt: Askeladden sitter med matpakka ved fjellfoten og ser opp. Fra en steindør som står på gløtt, henger en diger grå hånd ut et glitrende sengeteppe med sølv- og gullruter.

In the shadow at the foot of the Dark Mountain, Askeladden sits on a rock beside his beached trough with a half-eaten packed lunch, frozen mid-bite and staring up. Characters

Askeladden askeladden · Askeladden

Den yngste sønnen som virker undervurdert, men som møter farer med ro, rask tenkning og frekke bløffer.

A small, wiry lad of about sixteen, shorter than most, with a round face, rosy cheeks, bright brown eyes, a button nose, a dark-brown curly mop of hair and a cheeky gap-toothed grin. He wears a moss-green knitted jumper with brown leather elbow patches, worn jeans, thick oatmeal-coloured wool socks and scuffed brown hiking boots, and carries a small, worn brown canvas backpack.

Trollet trollet · the Troll

En gigantisk skogvokter som truer alle som hogger, lett å skremme med det den tror er overmenneskelig styrke, og drevet av stolthet.

A huge forest troll as big as a delivery van, grey and bristly all over, with cracked grey skin like an old pine trunk, a shaggy, bristly grey haystack of hair full of twigs and moss, a potato nose, eyes like two wet dark stones in a stream, an enormous mouth that stretches from ear to ear with big square teeth, long dangling arms, hands like upturned tree roots and a huge, round belly. He wears baggy, patched sackcloth trousers held up by braces of twisted roots.

Faren faren · the Father

Eldre bonde presset av gjeld og regninger, hard i ordene av bekymring, men med et sterkt ønske om å beholde gården.

A short, stocky, bow-legged old farmer of about seventy with a stiff back, a broad, weather-beaten, wrinkled face, a big bulbous nose, small eyes under shaggy grey eyebrows and a thick, bristly grey beard cut short and square. He wears reading glasses far down his nose, a patched grey-blue wool cardigan with horn buttons over a checked flannel shirt, brown work trousers with braces and thick grey wool socks.

Eldstebror eldstebror · the Eldest Brother

Den eldste sønnen som heller utsetter arbeidet, og som blir skremt fra skogen ved første møte med trollet.

A hulking, broad-shouldered young man of about twenty-two with a thick neck, a broad, flat face, a crooked nose, small pale-blue eyes, heavy black eyebrows and short, bristly black hair cropped close to his head. He wears a shaggy, sheepskin-lined sleeveless vest over a grey hoodie, baggy brown cargo trousers and heavy black boots.

Mellombror mellombror · the Middle Brother

Den mellomste sønnen, som skal starte et enda bedre firma enn broren, men som også slipper saga og løper fra trollet.

A thin, jittery young man of about twenty with a long neck, a narrow face, a long pointed nose, big worried eyes and frizzy light-brown hair. On his head sits a long, floppy, bright-yellow knitted beanie with a blue tassel. He wears a baggy blue hoodie, patched grey tracksuit trousers and wooden clogs.

Askeladden slo av saga og satte den fra seg. Så gikk han bort til sekken, uten å skynde seg, og fisket fram osten. Han holdt den opp så trollet kunne se den, hvit og rund og fortsatt våt. Så klemte han. Væsken sprutet ut mellom fingrene og dryppet ned i mosen.

Så klemte han. Væsken sprutet ut mellom fingrene og dryppet ned i mosen.

He holds up the small, round white cheese for the Troll to see and squeezes it, so that whey spurts out between his fingers and drips into the moss. The Troll stops dead above him, staring at the white stone and then at his own huge fist. Grey mist between the trunks.

The bear and the fox are wild animals without clothes: they walk on four legs, but can sit up and use their front paws like hands.

Characters

Bjørnen bjornen · the Bear

En stor, søvnig og rettferdig bjørn som lar seg overtale til å fiske med halen og ender opp med både kort hale og ufortjent skyld.

A huge, heavy, slow-moving and rather sleepy brown bear, taller than a man when he stands up, with thick, shaggy dark chocolate-brown winter fur, a broad head with small round ears, small, gentle black eyes under heavy brows, a short greyish-tan muzzle with a big black nose and a patient, slightly puzzled look. He has enormous flat paws with blunt claws and, unlike real bears, a long, fine, plume-like bushy tail that sweeps the snow behind him.

Den stubbrumpete bjørnen bjornen-stubbrumpet · the Stub-tailed Bear

Bjørnen etter isfisket, med bare en liten stump igjen bak. Han bærer ikke nag, han utsetter dvalen til over nyttår for julesmørets skyld, og han liker ting som er rettferdige.

The same huge, heavy, slow-moving and rather sleepy brown bear after his fishing trip: thick, shaggy dark chocolate-brown winter fur, a broad head with small round ears, small, gentle black eyes under heavy brows, a short greyish-tan muzzle with a big black nose, a patient, slightly puzzled look and enormous flat paws with blunt claws. His long tail is gone: all that is left is a tiny, round, fluffy stump on his big round bottom.

Reven reven · the Fox

En glatt og selvsikker rev som lærer bjørnen å fiske med halen og tar telefoner som aldri ringer, mens julesmøret forsvinner.

A slim, light-footed, long-legged red fox with sleek, bright flame-red winter fur, a snow-white chin, throat and chest, black lower legs and paws, tall pointed ears with black backs, narrow amber eyes with a sly sideways glance, a long pointed snout with long whiskers and a smooth, self-confident grin. His big, bushy red tail ends in a clean white tip.

modern · after paragraph 1
Bjørnen sto på parkeringsplassen og så på dem da reven kom luskende mellom bilene med en plastpose full av fisk. Fisken var pent buntet og pakket, akkurat slik den lå i disken på fiskebilen. Fiskebilen sto for øvrig også på parkeringsplassen. Det gjorde den hver torsdag.

Behind a roadside rest area, in long grass full of wildflowers, Askeladden sits with his knees up, his car keys dangling from one hand. The grey car park lies just beyond the grass.

Her straw-coloured hair hangs in two long plaits tied with grass-green ribbons, with little white and yellow flowers tucked into it. She wears a simple white dress to her ankles and tiny green shoes.

Story world: Present-day Norway in early summer. The family conglomerate began with one loom in a basement; now it owns three factories, a glass-fronted head office and a white villa by the water behind a wrought-iron gate. The rest area is a roadside café with a car park on a main road; behind it lies a meadow of long grass and wildflowers with round tussocks. Under one tussock is the Doll's home: a small room of grass with flowers growing from the ceiling and a single tiny chair. The tiny shirt is white linen, no longer than a car key. Her carriage is a polished silver spoon with a harness of sewing thread, pulled by two white mice. The old road is a narrow gravel road along a dark lake, squeezed between a rock wall and wet stones, with the new road high above.

This story's season, light and colours: Early summer with long, light days: fresh green grass and wildflowers (buttercups, clover, cow parsley) behind a grey tarmac car park and a low golden evening sun; the lake dark and cold under a drizzly grey sky; the homecoming at the villa in steady summer rain; the wedding on a pale, bright midsummer evening by the water. Accents: polished silver, sky blue and grass green.

A tiny young woman no taller than a mobile phone, perfectly formed with the natural proportions of a grown woman, slim and quick, with a small heart-shaped face, a tiny upturned nose, sparkling green eyes, rosy cheeks and a calm, bright smile. A tall, thin, elderly self-made industrialist of about seventy with narrow, sloping shoulders, a long, lined face, a long pointed nose, shrewd grey eyes under thin arched eyebrows and a neat, pointed grey goatee. He wears a deep-blue three-piece suit, a silk tie patterned with rosemaling flowers in red, white and yellow and polished dark-blue shoes, and keeps a small brass folding magnifier, a thread counter, in his waistcoat pocket.

A tall, broad-shouldered man of no clear age with a broad, weathered, kind face, a wide flat nose, calm sea-green eyes and long, straight black hair plastered wet down his back, with a strand of pondweed in it. Picture: Steady rain outside a white villa by the water. The Chairman stands on the top step under the porch roof, rubbing a black drop between his thumb and forefinger with a critical frown. Below him on the wet gravel stand the eleven brothers in soaked suits, each beside a sulky sweetheart in a big black hat, with black streaks running down all eleven of the sweethearts' faces. At the open wrought-iron gate behind them, Askeladden and the Grass Maiden have just arrived.

- the Chairman: A tall, thin, elderly self-made industrialist of about seventy with narrow, sloping shoulders, a long, lined face, a long pointed nose, shrewd grey eyes under thin arched eyebrows and a neat, pointed grey goatee. He wears a deep-blue three-piece suit, a silk tie patterned with rosemaling flowers in red, white and yellow and polished dark-blue shoes, and keeps a small brass folding magnifier, a thread counter, in his waistcoat pocket.
- Askeladden: A tall, gangly young man of twenty-five with long arms and legs, a long face with deep dimples when he smiles, warm hazel eyes, a straight nose and a thick copper-red mop cut straight round like a bowl. Her straw-coloured hair hangs in two long plaits tied with grass-green ribbons, with a small gold crown pinned on top. She wears a simple cornflower-blue dress to her ankles and green shoes.

The family conglomerate began with one loom in a basement; now it owns three factories, a glass-fronted head office and a white villa by the water behind a wrought-iron gate. The old road is a narrow gravel road along a dark lake, squeezed between a rock wall and wet stones, with the new road high above.

Askeladden og Dukken i gresset holdt bryllup ved vannet samme sommer. Den svarte hesten (den forheksede prinsen) hesten · the Black Horse

En svart hest med menneskeøyne som står bundet i trollets hus, snakker, hjelper gutten å flykte og vinne krigen, og til slutt ber om å bli satt fri fra trolldommen.

Trollet i den mørke bilen den-fremmede-mannen · the Stranger

Et troll i menneskeskikkelse, rolig og høflig i mørk frakk, som plukker opp gutten langs veien, forbyr ham fire dører i et halvferdig hus i granskogen og straffer ulydighet hardt.

An unusually tall, gaunt man who almost looks human: a long, craggy face with a stony grey complexion, a huge knobbly nose, small glinting black eyes that almost never blink under bushy iron-grey eyebrows, a wide, thin-lipped mouth set in a polite smile, big pointed ears and a short, bristly iron-grey beard. He has very long arms, huge knobbly hands and enormous flat feet in big black leather shoes, and wears a long black wool overcoat with large horn buttons, even indoors, over a dark-grey suit and a black roll-neck.

Prinsessa prinsessa · the Princess

Kongens datter, selvstendig og kvikk i joggesko, som ser gutten under lavparykken og holder fast på ham selv når hun får husarrest og mister telefonen.

A lively, quick-witted young woman of twenty-three with a round, dimpled face, a small nose, bright hazel eyes, fair rosy skin and two long, heavy dark-brown plaits tied with rose-pink hair elastics. She wears a loose rose-pink knitted jumper, wide light-blue jeans, chunky white trainers with pink laces and a slim silver necklace with a small pink stone.

Kongen kongen · the King

En streng og mektig konge i mørk dress med hvitt lommetørkle i brystlomma, som styrer kongsgården med kameraer og væpnede vakter og til slutt kjenner igjen sitt eget lommetørkle.

A broad, barrel-chested man in his fifties with a square, stern face, a big hooked nose, deep-set dark eyes under heavy black eyebrows and a thick, bushy black beard streaked with grey. He wears a dark bottle-green three-piece suit, a white shirt and a dark tie, a heavy gold signet ring, polished black shoes and, in his breast pocket, a crisp white handkerchief with a small crown embroidered in one corner.

#02 · den-fremmede-mannen, enkesonnen
modern · after paragraph 12
En dag sa han: «Nå reiser jeg bort i åtte dager. Du får være her alene så lenge. Men du får ikke gå inn i noen av disse fire rommene.» Han nikket mot enden av gangen, der fire dører sto tett i tett. «Gjør du det, tar jeg livet av deg når jeg kommer hjem.»

«Men du får ikke gå inn i noen av disse fire rommene.»

Behind the doors wait a whip braided from wild-rose twigs with thorns as long as drawing pins, a boulder the size of a loaf and an old tin army canteen, a trapdoor over a huge copper cauldron that boils with no heat under it, and a stable built inside the house. The ointment is grey and cold, in a small blue clay jar. A huge hollow linden stands in a green forest clearing near the royal estate.

Inside the Stranger's house: flat grey light through plastic sheeting and the warm glow of copper. The royal estate is cool glass, pale stone, clipped green hedges and black cars. Accents: wild-rose pink, rust orange and crisp white.

She wears a faded grey-blue fleece, mud-brown corduroy trousers and an apron. On her right foot is one brand-new, spotless white trainer; on her left foot, an old, scuffed grey one.

Datteren som later som hun er altfor travel til å rydde, og holder avstand for å bevare inntrykket av kontroll.

A cheeky young woman of about twenty-five with a long face, a sharp chin, a snub, upturned nose, big round brown eyes, rosy cheeks, a little rosebud mouth and thick black hair in two short, stiff plaits that poke straight out to the sides. She wears a faded brown hoodie and old grey jeans, and on her head a brand-new, bright emerald-green knitted beanie with a big fluffy white pom-pom.

In the small, worn farm kitchen, the Suitor sits politely on a mismatched chair with a coffee cup, in front of a plate of sweet buns. Beside him the Farmer rubs the edge of the scrubbed pine table with his one brand-new red sleeve, back and forth, back and forth, keeping his other arm stiffly behind his back. The Suitor watches the sleeve with raised eyebrows and a polite, puzzled smile. The wood stove glows in the corner.

Picture: In the small, worn farm kitchen, the Suitor sits politely on a mismatched chair with a coffee cup, in front of a plate of sweet buns. Beside him the Farmer rubs the edge of the scrubbed pine table with his one brand-new red sleeve, back and forth, back and forth, keeping his other arm stiffly behind his back. Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Farmer: A big, burly, barrel-chested farmer of about fifty-five with a broad, ruddy face, a small snub nose, twinkling little blue eyes, bushy brown eyebrows, a shock of unruly brown hair and a long brown beard that splits into two scraggly forks. He wears a faded, pilled dusty-red wool jumper with one brand-new sleeve knitted in almost the same red, only brighter and crisper, while the old sleeve has a hole at the elbow, patched work trousers and thick grey wool socks.
- the Suitor: A tall, gangly man of about twenty-seven with a round, eager face, apple-pink cheeks, a small blunt nose, hopeful pale-blue eyes, a nervous smile and neat butter-blond hair parted in the middle and combed down flat, except for one unruly cowlick at the back. He wears his best date outfit: a slightly too short cinnamon-brown corduroy blazer over a white shirt buttoned to the top, grey chinos and polished black boots, with a small brown leather shoulder bag.

Story world: Present-day Norway in late winter. The family's small farm lies at the very end of a narrow valley: an old white farmhouse with peeling paint and a roof patched with a big blue tarpaulin, a sagging red barn and a snowy yard with a rusty old tractor. The farm kitchen is small and worn smooth: a scrubbed pine table with mismatched chairs and two stools, a wood-burning stove, a rag rug on cracked linoleum, a coffee pot and a plate of sweet buns. Everything is old and faded except the family's three new things: the farmer's one new sleeve, the wife's one new trainer and the daughter's new beanie. The suitor carries a small brown leather shoulder bag.

This story's season, light and colours: Late winter at the end of a narrow valley: old grey snow, blue shadows and a pale, low sun. Inside the kitchen, warm light from the stove and a hanging lamp on faded pine and worn linoleum, from which the three new things shine out: a bright red sleeve, a spotless white trainer and an emerald-green beanie.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Giant Bird: An enormous bird so big that it nearly fills a castle courtyard, shaped a little like a giant gull, with a pale silver-grey back and wings with black tips, a snowy-white head and breast, kind dark eyes, a huge hooked golden-yellow beak and orange webbed feet. Its feathers look like twisted steel cables and strips of bark, and from the back of its neck rises one enormous, stiff copper-red feather as thick as a half-grown spruce.
- the Youngest Prince: A slim, brave prince of about twenty-four with a kind, open face, a fine straight nose, calm green-grey eyes, a ready smile and wavy dark-brown hair to his shoulders, a little stiff with salt. He wears a forest-green sailing jacket over a thick off-white Aran sweater, dark-grey trousers and brown deck boots, with a small gold pin shaped like a ship on his collar.

Setting:
- the Yacht: A large, sleek white sailing-and-motor yacht with a dark-blue stripe along the hull, one tall mast with white sails, a raised flybridge with a steering wheel, a cockpit with cushioned benches, a low steel rail around the deck, portholes along the side and a grey inflatable dinghy hanging from davits at the stern.

Story world: Present-day Norway and the open sea, over fourteen years. The King lives in a big city palace with a green palace park and naps on a leather sofa in his office. The twelve princes sail a large white sailing-and-motor yacht; the eleven older princes wear matching navy sailing jackets, and the eleven older princesses dress in different soft colours. On a small rocky island that is on no chart stands the Glass Castle, walled with tall glass arches between stone pillars. Far across the sea, the Dark Castle on a rocky shore holds the twelve-headed troll's gilded chamber. The little dog on the island is fluffy and white, with floppy brown ears. The crown cupboard is a waist-high blue wooden cupboard with red-and-white rosemaling, holding twelve small gold crowns on dark velvet. The iron boat is small and dark, with no motor, sail or oars.

This story's season, light and colours: Steel-grey and petrol-blue open sea, from three-day storms with white spray to sudden glassy calm under silver skies; night scenes in deep navy with warm lamp light. Back home, the crisp gold light of early autumn in the palace park, with yellowing birches and flags in the wind. Accents: Ridder Rød's bright red jacket, the prince's forest green and the gold of the crowns.

Characters

Den yngste kongssønnen den-yngste-kongssonnen · the Youngest Prince

Den yngste av tolv prinser, utholdende og observant, som alene tar sjansen, dreper uhyret, henter kronene og avslører løgnen når makt og frykt prøver å dysse ned sannheten.

A slim, brave prince of about twenty-four with a kind, open face, a fine straight nose, calm green-grey eyes, a ready smile and wavy dark-brown hair to his shoulders, a little stiff with salt. He wears a forest-green sailing jacket over a thick off-white Aran sweater, dark-grey trousers and brown deck boots, with a small gold pin shaped like a ship on his collar.

Sjømannen sjomannen · the Sailor

Den yngste kongssønnen i forkledning, i en stor, gammel sjømannsfrakk. Han later som han er en skipbrudden matros, og siden kommer han som selger med en kasse på ryggen.

A lean young seaman of about twenty-four in disguise, with a kind face, a fine straight nose, calm green-grey eyes and a few days' dark stubble, his wavy dark-brown hair pushed under a sun-bleached red watch cap. He wears a huge old navy sailor's greatcoat with tarnished buttons that hangs to his knees, canvas work trousers and salt-stained rubber boots.

Den yngste prinsessen den-yngste-prinsessen · the Youngest Princess

Den mest stille av de tolv, merket av fangenskapet og trusselen fra Ridder Rød, men modig nok til å peke ut sannheten når kronene kommer fram.

A small, slight young woman of about twenty-two with a round, solemn face, a short nose, deep-blue eyes under thick, level brows and a small, determined mouth. Her honey-brown hair is braided into a crown around her head. She wears a simple long cream-coloured knitted dress with a thin gold belt, and a little silver anchor pendant on a fine chain.

Fugl Dam fugl-dam · the Giant Bird

En fugl så stor at den nesten fyller gårdsplassen, med fjær som kabler og bark, som spiser fire tønner rug til frokost og flyr kongssønnen forbi yachten.

An enormous bird so big that it nearly fills a castle courtyard, shaped a little like a giant gull, with a pale silver-grey back and wings with black tips, a snowy-white head and breast, kind dark eyes, a huge hooked golden-yellow beak and orange webbed feet. Its feathers look like twisted steel cables and strips of bark, and from the back of its neck rises one enormous, stiff copper-red feather as thick as a half-grown spruce.

Ridder Rød ridder-rod · Ridder Rød

Styrmannen i den røde seilerjakken, som seiler fra den yngste kongssønnen, tar æren for redningen og sender ut pressemeldingen om forlovelsen selv.

A tall, barrel-chested, vain man of about forty with a big square jaw, a cleft chin, a short straight nose held high, small, cold pale-blue eyes and a proud, camera-ready smirk. He has short flame-red hair and a short, pointed flame-red beard. He always wears the same bright red offshore sailing jacket with the collar turned up, over white trousers, navy deck shoes and a heavy gold diver's watch.

Storetrollet med tolv hoder storetrollet · the Great Troll

Sjefen til trollet på øya. Han sitter pyntet som til fest i en praktfull sal, med tolv hoder som snorker i tolv forskjellige takter, mens prinsessene luser ham.

A huge, hulking troll about three times as tall as a man, with rust-red, warty skin, a broad, sagging barrel of a body, very long arms that hang to the floor and short bowed legs. On his thick neck sits a bunch of exactly twelve small heads, packed tightly together like a bunch of turnips, each with a knobbly nose, droopy ears and a wispy tuft of straw-coloured hair. He is dressed for a party in a dark-blue velvet dinner jacket, heavy gold chains and rings on every finger.

Trollet på øya trollet-pa-oya · the Island Troll

Et stort og stygt troll på en benk i slottet av stein og glass. Han gir kongssønnen sverdet og flasken, for han er lei av sjefen sin.

A huge, strange troll about three times as tall as a man, shaped like a giant sack of flour, with sloping shoulders, a small head, a big soft belly, short legs and huge webbed feet like a duck's. His skin is a weathered, ruddy tan. He has a nose as long as a cucumber, small unblinking amber eyes, big ears like cabbage leaves and a stiff crest of dark-brown hair standing straight up like a brush. He wears a baggy mulberry-purple knitted jumper and grey work trousers.

Trollkongen (øya-slottet) trollkongen · the Troll King

Det store, stygge trollet på benken i slottet av stein og glass, som gir kongssønnen sverdet og flasken for å bli kvitt sjefen sin, og som går i dress og krone når han selv blir konge.

A huge troll king about three times as tall as a man, shaped like a giant sack of flour, with sloping shoulders, a small head, a big soft belly and huge webbed feet like a duck's, weathered ruddy-tan skin, a nose as long as a cucumber, small amber eyes, ears like cabbage leaves and a brush-like crest of dark-brown hair. He wears an enormous charcoal suit with a mulberry-purple tie, gold chains across his waistcoat, a fur cape on his shoulders and a gold crown.

Trolldatteren trolldatteren · the Troll's Daughter

Trollets datter. Først er hun en liten, våt hund på en øy, så en vakker og alvorlig ung kvinne som sender faren sin lange blikk. I mange år syr hun skjorter og sengetøy til kongssønnen.

A willowy young woman of about twenty-two with pale, milky skin, a long, narrow face, a tiny pointed nose, big silvery-grey eyes, a serious, unimpressed look and long, pale-blonde hair that drifts around her as if she were under water. She wears a long apricot-coloured knitted dress and a thin silver bracelet, and goes barefoot.

Kongen kongen · the King

Prinsessenes far, som helst vil ha de tolv døtrene rundt seg hele tiden, og som slutter å sove middag da de blir borte.

A small, wiry, elderly king with a narrow, kind, crinkly face, a small sharp nose, twinkling blue eyes, wisps of silver hair and a long silver-grey beard braided into two plaits tied with little gold rings. He wears a dark navy suit with a turquoise tie and a silver tie pin shaped like a fish, and soft grey felt slippers.

Den gamle damen damen · the Nosy Old Lady

En nysgjerrig gammel dame i et skjevt hus ved havnen, som spør og graver og ringer alle hun kjenner med nyheten.

A short, bustling old lady with a plump little body on thin legs, like a robin, and a long neck that she cranes forward to see everything. She has a sharp little chin, a beaky nose, big curious eyes magnified by thick, round glasses and wispy white hair scraped into a tiny topknot like an onion. She wears a lavender cardigan over a flowered dress, an orange knitted scarf and a patched brown apron with a mobile phone in its deep pocket.

modern · after paragraph 1
Det eneste de hadde for seg selv, var middagsluren hans. Hver dag etter lunsj la kongen seg på sofaen på kontoret og sov i tjue minutter, og de tjue minuttene brukte prinsessene til å gå tur i slottsparken. Uten livvakter og uten ham.

Past the open door, twelve young women tiptoe out towards the green palace park beyond the tall windows: eleven sisters in different soft colours, and last of all the Youngest Princess, glancing back at him with a small smile, one finger to her lips. No bodyguards in sight.

Om kvelden bar han inn sakene sine, og han hadde knapt fått dem inn før damen, som ikke likte noe bedre enn nytt å løpe rundt med, begynte å spørre. Hvem var han? Hvor kom han fra? Create the cover illustration for an illustrated book of modern fairy tales, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: Night on a gravel farm road, in the orange beam of a single yard light. Sooty Giske stands in the middle of the road with her arms flung wide and her bald head gleaming, shouting something happily at the top of her voice. Behind her, the Skinny Thief and the Plump Thief crouch with their sacks on their backs, clapping their hands over their ears and looking around in panic at the dark farmhouses.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Sooty Giske: Giske after the prank: the same very tall, strong farmhand of about thirty with extremely long legs, a long oval face, a wide mouth, a small turned-up nose and bright hazel eyes, but her head is shaved completely bald. Her bald scalp, face and arms are smeared with greasy black chimney soot that shines with tallow, streaky and patchy like a chimney sweep's. Her plum-purple fleece sweater and dark-green work trousers are streaked with black, and she wears black rubber boots and a bunch of keys on a carabiner.
- the Skinny Thief: A skinny, jittery petty thief of about thirty, a head shorter than Giske, with a long pale face, a long pointy nose, big frightened eyes, a wispy ginger goatee and lank hair under a floppy black beanie. He wears a charcoal hoodie that is too short in the arms, grey tracksuit trousers and worn-out trainers, and carries a big canvas sack on his back.
- the Plump Thief: A short, round, nervous petty thief of about forty, much shorter than Giske, with a round red face, puffy cheeks, a stubbly double chin, tiny eyes, a big bushy black moustache and a bald head under a brown flat cap. He wears a mustard-brown hoodie stretched tight over his belly, baggy jeans and big unlaced work boots, with a coil of rope over his shoulder and a canvas sack on his back.

The widower's smallholding is a red farmhouse with a kitchen window over a gravel yard, a shed and a field of tall, ripe industrial hemp at the bottom of the land. The farms have sheep barns built wall to wall with the farmhouse, solar panels on the barn roofs, goose houses and orange yard lights. The big farm at the forest edge has a farm shop and an old stabbur, a timber storehouse on stilts full of cured hams, sausages and flatbread. The turnip field lies on a hillside above a dark bog of tussocks. Giske's soot is greasy chimney soot mixed with tallow.

Characters

Giske giske · Giske

Langbeint gårdshjelp som vil gifte seg med sjefen sin, blir barbert skallet og smurt inn med talg og sot mens hun sover, og konkluderer rolig med at hun må være fanden.

A very tall, strong farmhand of about thirty, a head taller than any man, with extremely long legs and big hands rough from farm work. She has a long oval face, rosy weathered cheeks, a wide eager smile, a small turned-up nose, bright hazel eyes and flaxen hair wound into a tall bun on top of her head. She wears a plum-purple fleece sweater with the sleeves pushed up, dark-green work trousers with knee pockets, black rubber boots and a big bunch of keys on a carabiner at her belt.

Giske som fanden giske-skallet · Sooty Giske

Giske etter spøken: barbert skallet, blank av talg og svart av sot, så ikke engang mobilen kjenner henne igjen. Når hun ikke er Giske, må hun vel være fanden.

Giske after the prank: the same very tall, strong farmhand of about thirty with extremely long legs, a long oval face, a wide mouth, a small turned-up nose and bright hazel eyes, but her head is shaved completely bald. Her bald scalp, face and arms are smeared with greasy black chimney soot that shines with tallow, streaky and patchy like a chimney sweep's. Her plum-purple fleece sweater and dark-green work trousers are streaked with black, and she wears black rubber boots and a bunch of keys on a carabiner.

Enkemannen enkemannen · the Widower

Konfliktsky småbruker som heller barberer og sotsverter gårdshjelpen sin enn å si nei til henne rett ut.

A skinny, stooped smallholder of about fifty with a long, narrow, tired face, heavy-lidded eyes, a long crooked nose, hollow cheeks, a scruffy salt-and-pepper chin beard and thin dark hair combed flat, with cheap reading glasses pushed up on his forehead. He wears a pilled heather-brown fleece jacket over a faded checked flannel shirt, baggy grey work trousers and green rubber clogs, and always looks as if he would rather be somewhere else.

Den tynne tyven tyven-tynn · the Skinny Thief

Den ene av de to småtyvene fra bygda som lever av det som ikke er boltet fast. Han er tynn og skvetten, og det er han som hysjer mest.

A skinny, jittery petty thief of about thirty, a head shorter than Giske, with a long pale face, a long pointy nose, big frightened eyes, a wispy ginger goatee and lank hair under a floppy black beanie. He wears a charcoal hoodie that is too short in the arms, grey tracksuit trousers and worn-out trainers, and carries a big canvas sack on his back.

Den tykke tyven tyven-tykk · the Plump Thief

Den andre småtyven. Han er liten og rund, har ikke spist ordentlig siden tirsdag og vil aller helst ikke bli tatt.

A short, round, nervous petty thief of about forty, much shorter than Giske, with a round red face, puffy cheeks, a stubbly double chin, tiny eyes, a big bushy black moustache and a bald head under a brown flat cap. He wears a mustard-brown hoodie stretched tight over his belly, baggy jeans and big unlaced work boots, with a coil of rope over his shoulder and a canvas sack on his back.

Bonden med sauefjøset bonden · the Sheep Farmer

Bonden med solcellepanel på låvetaket og en drone som teller sauene. Han har aldri trodd på noe han ikke kan se, helt til noe langt og svart kommer farende ut av sauefjøset hans.

A lean, wiry sheep farmer of about forty-five with a bony, hollow-cheeked face, a hooked nose, bristly grey stubble, startled round eyes and wild, tousled grey hair, just woken from sleep. He wears only a faded grey T-shirt and baggy navy-blue boxer shorts, with bare skinny legs and bare feet, and a chunky black sports watch on one wrist.

Bonden med nepeåkeren nepebonden · the Turnip Farmer

Bonden som eier nepeåkeren. Han har ligget våken og lest om fanden i bygdegruppa hele natta, og han lover presten en kalvestek for å få ham med ut på myra.

A short, sturdy, bow-legged farmer of about fifty with a square, weather-beaten face, a big bristly chestnut moustache, round startled eyes, bushy eyebrows and wiry grey hair sticking up under a wide, frayed straw hat. He wears a rust-orange quilted vest over a blue-striped pyjama top, grey work trousers pulled on over his pyjama bottoms and green rubber boots.

Presten presten · the Priest

Sokneprest som blir hentet ut i tøfler og strikkelue en søndag morgen for å binde fanden, lokket av en kalvestek, og havner i myra.

A very round, heavy parish priest of about sixty-five with a big belly, short legs, a pink, jowly, clean-shaven face, puffy sleepy eyes, bushy white eyebrows and a fringe of white curls under a red-and-white striped knitted hat with a pompom. He wears a crumpled white pyjama shirt stuffed into black trousers he has pulled on in a hurry and a pair of blue felt slippers, and carries a small black book.

Story world: Present-day Norway in July. Gjertrud's lefse shack stands alone by a county road: a small, low wooden hut painted red, with one window, a bench outside and a gravel lay-by. Inside is one room with a glass-fronted counter, a big round electric griddle on a steel table, a floury worktop with a rolling pin, and a steel extractor hood above the griddle whose fan hums from opening to closing time; its duct runs up into the hut's old brick chimney, black with twenty-two years of grease and soot. The lefser are big, thin, round flatbreads, pale with brown speckles, and every one Gjertrud rolls, however tiny the scrap of dough, spreads until it covers the whole griddle.

This story's season, light and colours: A hot, still July afternoon: pale dusty gravel, bleached grass and tall purple lupins along the county road, a hazy white sky and dark spruce behind. Inside the shack: flat, cool daylight from the window, brushed steel, the orange glow of the griddle and pale flour. Accents: the scarlet knitted hat and the greasy black of old soot.

Gjertrud gjertrud · Gjertrud

Eier av et lite veikantkjøkken som baker lefser; hun sier ja med munnen, men holder igjen med hendene, og blir fanget av sin egen smålighet.

A stout, square-built woman of about fifty-five with a square jaw, pinched thin lips, a sharp little upturned nose and small darting black eyes. Her iron-grey hair is tucked away under a tall, pointed, bright-scarlet knitted hat with a tassel, pulled down to her eyebrows. She wears a white short-sleeved work tunic, a flour-dusted white apron, dark-grey trousers and white clogs.

Jesus jesus · Jesus

En stille, sliten vandrer som ber høflig om en liten smakebit og svarer med hard rettferdighet når godhet nektes.

A very old, tall and slightly stooped man with a long, gentle face, deep-set, kind blue-grey eyes, a high wrinkled forehead, thin snow-white hair to his shoulders and a long white beard that reaches his belt. He wears a long, plain, hooded brown cloak over a simple undyed tunic, both dusty to the knees, and worn leather sandals, and carries a tall, knobbly wooden staff. No halo.

Reisekameraten som følger etter, sulten og trøtt, og blir vitne til både mirakel og straff uten å styre utfallet.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):

- Jesus: A very old, tall and slightly stooped man with a long, gentle face, deep-set, kind blue-grey eyes, a high wrinkled forehead, thin snow-white hair to his shoulders and a long white beard that reaches his belt. Story world: Present-day Norway in July. Gjertrud's lefse shack stands alone by a county road: a small, low wooden hut painted red, with one window, a bench outside and a gravel lay-by. Inside is one room with a glass-fronted counter, a big round electric griddle on a steel table, a floury worktop with a rolling pin, and a steel extractor hood above the griddle whose fan hums from opening to closing time; its duct runs up into the hut's old brick chimney, black with twenty-two years of grease and soot. The lefser are big, thin, round flatbreads, pale with brown speckles, and every one Gjertrud rolls, however tiny the scrap of dough, spreads until it covers the whole griddle.

This story's season, light and colours: A hot, still July afternoon: pale dusty gravel, bleached grass and tall purple lupins along the county road, a hazy white sky and dark spruce behind. Inside the shack: flat, cool daylight from the window, brushed steel, the orange glow of the griddle and pale flour. Accents: the scarlet knitted hat and the greasy black of old soot.

The Boy calmly brushes dust off his jacket sleeve.

Om gutten som gikk til nordavinden og krevde melet tilbake guttnord · 10/10 pictures

Derfra var det en halvtime å gå, i motvind.

A narrow road runs out along a bare, windswept headland to a low grey house lashed to the rock with steel cables, at the very edge of a white-capped grey sea. On the steps of the house far ahead stands the North Wind, his huge hooded jacket flapping like a sail and fraying into cloud.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):

- the North Wind: A very tall, gaunt old man, head and shoulders taller than anyone else, with a broad, weathered face, round puffed-out cheeks, icy-blue eyes, great bushy white eyebrows, a moustache like drifted snow and a long, frosty white beard that always streams sideways. He wears a huge storm-grey hooded anorak with the hood up, flapping like a sail, whose hem and sleeves fray into swirling grey cloud and snowflakes, so that nobody can tell where the jacket ends and the weather begins.

Story world: Present-day Norway in raw late autumn. The boy and his mother live in a small flat in a grey block of flats with open-air galleries along each floor, a storage shed at the end of the gallery, and a courtyard and car park between the blocks. A long bus ride north ends at a lonely road junction with a roadside motel and café, its red and blue neon glowing in the wet dark, rubbish containers at the back and a small goat pen behind the car park. From the last bus stop a road runs half an hour out onto a bare headland above the sea, to the North Wind's low grey house, lashed to the rock with steel cables. The oat flour comes in plastic bags. The magic cloth is a plain square white tablecloth. The stick is an old wooden walking stick with a curved handle.

Gutten gutten · the Boy

En sta og rettferdig tenåring som nekter å godta at de fattige skal miste det lille de har, og som tør å konfrontere både naturkrefter og mennesker som utnytter andre.

A small, slight boy of about fourteen with a narrow, pale face, cheeks rosy from the cold, big ears that stick out, bright blue eyes, a determined frown and white-blond hair standing up in tufts. He wears a cheap navy windbreaker zipped to the chin over a grey knitted jumper several sizes too big, baggy charcoal tracksuit bottoms, muddy canvas sneakers, a long brown knitted scarf and a battered dark-green backpack.

Moren moren · the Mother

En utslitt, skrøpelig alenemor i en liten leilighet som bare ønsker ro og mat på bordet, og som blir guttens moralske anker.

A thin, worn-out woman of about sixty, a little stooped from her aching hips, with a long, gentle, deeply lined face, tired grey eyes, a thin mouth and one eyebrow often raised in doubt. Her grey hair hangs in one thin braid over her shoulder. She wears a faded plum-coloured fleece top, a darned brown knitted cardigan, grey tracksuit trousers and felt slippers.

Nordavinden nordavinden · the North Wind

En barsk, nesten menneskelig vindskikkelse som virker like gammel som været selv—knapp i replikkene, men i stand til å gi gaver som kan endre liv.

A very tall, gaunt old man, head and shoulders taller than anyone else, with a broad, weathered face, round puffed-out cheeks, icy-blue eyes, great bushy white eyebrows, a moustache like drifted snow and a long, frosty white beard that always streams sideways. Motellverten motellverten · the Motel Owner

En grådig og opportunistisk motelleier som ser magi som en forretningsmulighet, og som ikke nøler med å stjele for å få en evig fordel.

A tall, gangly motel owner of about fifty with a long, narrow face, a much too wide, toothy smile, small, hard, glittering eyes, a long pointed chin, restless hands and oily black hair twisted into one big curl on his forehead. He wears a wine-red quilted vest over a white shirt with rolled-up sleeves, dark jeans, a black belt bag heavy with coins and keys, and scuffed brown loafers.

Bukken bukken · the Billy Goat

En helt vanlig bukk å se på, som gjør gullmynter når gutten sier «Min bukk, gjør penger».

A small, sturdy billy goat about the size of a large dog, with a shaggy snow-white coat, a light-grey face with a little pointed grey beard, bright amber eyes with slot-shaped pupils, short, curved, ridged horns, a stubby tail and neat black hooves. Around his neck he wears a red leather collar hung with two small brass bells, with a length of blue nylon rope tied to it.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):

- the Mother: A thin, worn-out woman of about sixty, a little stooped from her aching hips, with a long, gentle, deeply lined face, tired grey eyes, a thin mouth and one eyebrow often raised in doubt. Story world: Present-day Norway in raw late autumn. The boy and his mother live in a small flat in a grey block of flats with open-air galleries along each floor, a storage shed at the end of the gallery, and a courtyard and car park between the blocks. From the last bus stop a road runs half an hour out onto a bare headland above the sea, to the North Wind's low grey house, lashed to the rock with steel cables. The oat flour comes in plastic bags. The magic cloth is a plain square white tablecloth. The stick is an old wooden walking stick with a curved handle.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Rooster: A sleek, swaggering rooster of ordinary size with jet-black plumage that shimmers beetle-green, a tall, jagged scarlet comb, long scarlet wattles, small white earlobes, fiery orange eyes, a sharp slate-grey beak, slate-grey legs and a fountain of curving green-black sickle feathers for a tail. He carries himself like the man of the yard, chest out and head high, with a phone in a black case tucked under one wing.
- the Cow: A gentle, sturdy Norwegian farm cow with a glossy reddish-brown coat, a broad white stripe along her back and down her tail, a white belly, white-speckled legs, a pink nose, big, calm brown eyes with long lashes and two short, pale, upward-curving horns. She wears a blue rope halter with a short lead rope, and chews her cud slowly, unimpressed by everything around her.
- the Cuckoo: A slim, sleek common cuckoo, smaller than the rooster, with a smooth ash-blue-grey head, back and wings, a white belly finely barred with thin dark stripes, a long, rounded dark-grey tail edged with little white spots, bright yellow rings around his round eyes, a short, slightly curved dark beak with a yellow base and small yellow feet. One tuft of feathers always sticks up at the back of his head.

The Rooster, the Cuckoo and the Black Grouse are ordinary-sized birds who live like neighbours around the same small farmyard: three old wooden houses, one red, one yellow and one white, around a gravel yard with a barn, a flagpole and a few round, white-wrapped silage bales. They have phones, a group chat and one cow between them, bought on a Saturday from a seller in the car park of a shopping centre: a flat grey tarmac lot with painted parking bays, trolleys and rows of cars in front of a big, windowless shopping centre. The birds and the cow wear no clothes.

Accents: the Rooster's scarlet comb, the Cow's russet coat and her blue rope halter.

Hanen hanen · the Rooster

A sleek, swaggering rooster of ordinary size with jet-black plumage that shimmers beetle-green, a tall, jagged scarlet comb, long scarlet wattles, small white earlobes, fiery orange eyes, a sharp slate-grey beak, slate-grey legs and a fountain of curving green-black sickle feathers for a tail. Gjøken gjoken · the Cuckoo

Lettantennelig og opportunistisk, som svarer umiddelbart og prøver å sikre seg i det minste en «halv ku».

Århanen arhanen · the Black Grouse

Den mest sindige av dem, som prøver å megle med fornuft og rettferdighet, mobil i hånda som om han vurderer å lese opp en avtale.

Per waits in a rented bedsit in a shabby block of flats behind the railway. Herreper drives a low, dark, gleaming sports car; the King rides in a long black car with advisers, security men with earpieces and four Royal Guard riders carrying small Norwegian flags. Far away lies the Silver Estate, where everything inside is gold, even the light switches. The pot is a black cast-iron pot, the griddle a big, flat, round iron griddle.

Per per · Per

Yngste bror uten arv og uten plan, som lar seg bære av kattens dristige opplegg og lærer å spille rollen som «Herreper» i en moderne verden.

A gangly, gentle young man of about twenty-three with a long neck, long arms, a kind oval face, soft brown eyes, a straight nose, a shy smile, a few days' stubble and chestnut hair tied back in a short ponytail. He wears his late father's old grey wool jacket, too broad in the shoulders and too long in the sleeves, over a washed-out blue flannel shirt, baggy brown cargo trousers, old canvas sneakers and a shapeless oatmeal beanie.

Herreper herreper · Herreper

Per i mørkeblå dress og blanke sko, med en lav, mørk bil som katten har skaffet. Alt kongen viser ham, har han finere hjemme.

Katten katten · the Cat

Den unge kvinnen kvinnen · the Young Woman

Katten i sin egen skikkelse. Trollet tok huset og landet hennes og gjorde henne til katt. Nå er hun fri og kan gjøre som hun vil.

A graceful young woman of about twenty-three with a small pointed chin, high cheekbones, almond-shaped green-gold eyes like a cat's, a little upturned nose and a calm, direct gaze. Her very long, straight hair is silver-grey and falls to her waist. She wears a long, plain white dress with long sleeves and a high neck, and goes barefoot.

Kongen kongen · the King

En moderne monark vant til å bli beundret, som både lar seg imponere og provosere når en ukjent «Herreper» viser tegn på å være rikere enn ham.

A short, very fat king of about sixty with a round, shiny bald head, bulging cheeks, a red nose, small beady eyes, a grumpy look and a huge drooping grey walrus moustache that hides his mouth. On ordinary days he wears a dark plum-coloured three-piece suit stretched tight over his enormous belly, a white shirt, a gold tie clip, a heavy gold signet ring and polished oxblood shoes.

Trollet (den skjulte eieren) trollet · the Troll

En truende, usett makt bak godset—en brutal «eier» som opptrer som et monster i moderne forkledning og som katten til slutt lurer i dagslyset.

A colossal troll about four times a man's height, round-shouldered and heavy, with long, matted, oatmeal-beige fur covering his head and face, two round yellow eyes that glow like lanterns, a big potato nose and a broad mouth with two blunt buck teeth. His huge bare hands are grey as stone. He wears a gigantic, worn olive-drab work jacket with the hood up and baggy grey work trousers, and goes barefoot on broad, hairy feet.

Story world: Present-day eastern Norway in late summer. Per's family's small, worn wooden house stands empty at the end of a gravel track. Herreper drives a low, dark, gleaming sports car; the King rides in a long black car with advisers, security men with earpieces and four Royal Guard riders carrying small Norwegian flags. Far away lies the Silver Estate, where everything inside is gold, even the light switches. The pot is a black cast-iron pot, the griddle a big, flat, round iron griddle.

Far off, past a main road and a great spruce forest, stands the big white manor everyone calls the castle, with a park, a stone-edged spring under an old oak, a chapel, an east wing and a grassy field below the park. Jomfru Maria (gudmoren) gudmoren · the Godmother

En elegant, tidløs velgjører som betaler dåpen, oppdrar barnet i et stort stille hus og setter tre forbudte dører som prøve; hun tar barna for å speile sorg og straff, men gir til slutt alt tilbake.

A tall, slender, serene woman who looks about thirty-five, with an oval face, calm dark-brown eyes, a straight nose, softly arched dark brows and a gentle, grave smile, and a faint, soft glow always around her head. A deep-blue silk shawl covers her dark hair. She wears a long, light cream wool coat over a deep-blue dress, a small silver lily brooch on the lapel, spotless pale-grey shoes and a simple pale leather handbag on her arm.

Jenta som sjuåring jenta-liten · the Little Girl

Jenta som vokser opp i gudmorens store, stille hus. Da hun er sju, får hun nøkkelen med den lille brikken, og etter fire dager åpner hun den første døra.

A small girl of seven with a heart-shaped face, a button nose, big curious grey-green eyes, rosy cheeks and long ash-blonde hair in a single plait with a coral-pink hair tie. She wears a peach-coloured cotton dress with short sleeves over white leggings and red canvas sneakers, and a small old key with a little round tag on a coral-pink ribbon round her neck.

Jenta som tolvåring jenta · the Girl

Jenta når hun er tolv. Hun lover å holde seg unna den andre døra, og hun mener det, men hun tenker på den hele tida.

A slender, long-legged girl of twelve with a heart-shaped face, a button nose, big grey-green eyes and a thoughtful frown, and long ash-blonde hair in a loose ponytail with a coral-pink hair tie. She wears an oversized peach-coloured hoodie, grey joggers and scuffed white trainers, with the small old key with its round tag on a coral-pink cord round her neck.

Den unge kvinnen (den stumme bruden) den-unge-kvinnen · the Young Woman

Jenta som de fattige foreldrene lar gudmoren ta med seg etter dåpen, og som mister stemmen, gifter seg med prinsen i en brudekjole fra loftet og må se tre nyfødte barn forsvinne.

A strikingly lovely young woman of seventeen with a heart-shaped face, a small nose, large grey-green eyes with dark lashes and a soft, silent mouth. Her long ash-blonde hair falls loose to her waist. She wears a simple, long ivory wedding dress with a lace bodice and long lace sleeves, and a long, thin tulle veil pinned in her hair, and she goes barefoot.

Prinsen (arvingen) prinsen · the Prince

En ung arving i et hus alle i distriktet kaller slottet; han finner henne i treet over kilden, insisterer på å gifte seg med henne og prøver å beskytte henne med vakter og kameraer som likevel ikke virker.

A tall, easy-going young man of about twenty-five with a long, open face, a strong nose, warm hazel eyes that crinkle when he smiles, wavy light-brown hair swept back to his collar and a short, neatly trimmed light-brown beard. He wears a teal-blue wool overshirt over a pale-grey T-shirt, charcoal chinos, brown suede boots and a thin silver signet ring.

Prinsens mor prinsens-mor · the Prince's Mother

En kjølig og mistenksom matriark som ser den stumme bruden som en trussel, driver fram dommen om straff, men endrer seg når barna kommer tilbake og sannheten blir sagt høyt.

A short, stout, stiff-backed woman of about sixty-five with a round double chin, a haughty little upturned nose, small sharp black eyes, thin pencilled eyebrows and pursed lips. Her silver-white hair is set high in stiff curls. She wears a high-necked deep-purple wool dress with a white collar, a string of large pearls, a heavy gold ring with a red stone, and gold-rimmed glasses on a thin gold chain that she lifts to peer at people.

She wears a simple, long ivory wedding dress with a lace bodice and long lace sleeves, and a long, thin tulle veil pinned in her hair, and she goes barefoot.
- the Prince: A tall, easy-going young man of about twenty-five with a long, open face, a strong nose, warm hazel eyes that crinkle when he smiles, wavy light-brown hair swept back to his collar and a short, neatly trimmed light-brown beard. He wears a teal-blue wool overshirt over a pale-grey T-shirt, charcoal chinos, brown suede boots and a thin silver signet ring.
- the Prince's Mother: A short, stout, stiff-backed woman of about sixty-five with a round double chin, a haughty little upturned nose, small sharp black eyes, thin pencilled eyebrows and pursed lips. Her silver-white hair is set high in stiff curls. She wears a high-necked deep-purple wool dress with a white collar, a string of large pearls, a heavy gold ring with a red stone, and gold-rimmed glasses on a thin gold chain that she lifts to peer at people.

Setting:
- the Bonfire Field: A wide, grassy field below the park of a big white manor, sloping gently down towards dark forest, with an avenue of old trees along one side. In the middle of the field, a tall midsummer bonfire of old planks, pallets and branches is stacked high and tight around a tall wooden pole.

Story world: Present-day rural eastern Norway. The poor family rents a small, shabby house at the end of a muddy gravel road where the forest begins. The godmother drives a long dark car with two silent men in dark coats in the back seat. Her house is a big, old, quiet wooden villa with long, cold corridors and tall windows; three plain white doors stand side by side at the end of the longest corridor. The star is small, white and sharp; the moon huge, cold and silver-white; the sun a glowing golden ball. Far off, past a main road and a great spruce forest, stands the big white manor everyone calls the castle, with a park, a stone-edged spring under an old oak, a chapel, an east wing and a grassy field below the park. The key has a small round tag.

This story's season, light and colours: Rain and mud at a grey dusk at the start; inside the old villa, cold grey-white corridors lit by the star's sharp white, the moon's cold silver and the sun's molten gold; then a long, luminous Norwegian summer: pale green park lawns, dark spruce, white nights and a golden midsummer dusk. Accents: the godmother's deep blue and the ivory of the wedding dress.

Art style: Contemporary Scandinavian editorial illustration: flat, graphic shapes with subtle risograph grain and a little hand-drawn texture, clean confident lines and a limited palette of spot inks led by deep petrol blue, with fjord teal, lingonberry red, honey mustard, sage green, warm paper off-white and ink charcoal, like the pages of a risograph-printed book, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, in the cool, clear Nordic light of today. Present-day Norway: fjord towns, suburbs, farms with tractors, cabins, ferries, roadside petrol stations, offices and flats, grey rain and bright snow, with people in modern clothes such as rain jackets, knitted sweaters, hoodies, suits and work wear. The magic of the tale appears plainly in this everyday world: trolls, talking animals and enchantments look real and slightly absurd, drawn in the same flat style. Every character has their own face, build, age, hair and clothes exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Dry humour, careful composition with one focal point and plenty of negative space. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Kari Trestakk katrast · 22/22 pictures

Kari rir på den blågrå oksen mot skogene av kobber, sølv og gull.

Alt: Kari sitter på ryggen til en stor, blågrå okse på en lyngås i soloppgangen. Bak dem ligger en motorvei og kraftlinjer, foran dem tre skoger av kobber, sølv og gull.

On a high heather ridge at sunrise, Kari rides on the Blue-Grey Ox's back in her green work jacket, holding on to his horns, her copper hair blowing in the wind. Far behind them run a thin grey motorway and a line of pylons; far ahead, three magic forests lie one behind another in the valleys: shining copper, glittering silver and glowing gold. The ox strides forward, calm and strong, and Kari gazes at the forests in wonder.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Kari: A slender young woman of about nineteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair tied back loosely with a strip of blue cloth. She wears a faded green work jacket over a sage-green hoodie, worn jeans, black rubber boots and a grey knitted scarf, and carries a battered old steel thermos.
- the Blue-Grey Ox: A huge, gentle ox, taller at the shoulder than a grown man, with a glossy, spotless blue-grey coat that stays clean and shining in any weather, a paler grey muzzle, big, soft dark-brown eyes with long lashes, two long, smooth cream-white horns curving upwards, large soft ears, a curly tuft of darker blue-grey hair between the horns, a long tail ending in a navy-blue tassel and dark grey hooves. Calm, kind and very strong.

Story world: Present-day Norway. Kari's father, the king, lives in a palace of glass and concrete at the end of a long avenue of trees, half home and half offices, with garages, a staff car park and a red barn for the royal cows, which graze on the mountain behind. The blue-grey ox keeps a small, folded white cloth in his left ear; spread on the grass, it sets itself with food. Far beyond the last motorways, power lines and paths lie three magic forests: one of copper, one of silver with leaves as thin as razor blades, and one of gold that drips from the leaves. Each troll wears a curved cow horn of healing salve at its belt. At the journey's end, a dark cliff on a windswept plateau looks down on another kingdom's castle with towers and an old stone church. The gold shoes are small, pointed and shining.

This story's season, light and colours: Crisp early autumn: high, pale-blue skies over grey concrete and glass, yellowing birches and purple heather on the windswept plateau, with the ox's glossy blue-grey as the strongest colour until the forests blaze in copper, frost-silver and molten gold. The castle kitchen lies under flat fluorescent light; the church Sundays are bright and windy.

Characters

Kari kari · Kari

Kongsdattera som stemora tar mobilen og maten fra og setter til å gjete kyrne, og som får en god venn i den blågrå oksen.

A slender young woman of about nineteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair tied back loosely with a strip of blue cloth. She wears a faded green work jacket over a sage-green hoodie, worn jeans, black rubber boots and a grey knitted scarf, and carries a battered old steel thermos.

Kari Trestakk kari-trestakk · Kari Trestakk

En kongsdatter som stemora setter til å gjete kyr, og som rømmer med den blågrå oksen og tar oppvaskjobb på et fremmed slott i en trestakk av bord og filler.

A slender young woman of about nineteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows and a dimple in her chin, her face and hands black with soot and her long, wavy copper hair in a messy braid. Over her green work jacket and jeans she wears the trestakk: a stiff, bell-shaped shell of thin, grey-brown wooden boards laced together with rope and rags, reaching from her neck to her shins, and black rubber boots.

Kari i kobberkjolen kari-kobberkjole · Kari in the Copper Dress

Kari den første søndagen, i en enkel kjole som skinner som kobberskogen, med hansker og hest fra mannen i berget.

A slender young woman of about nineteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair falling loose down her back. She wears a long, simply cut gown of shining copper silk that glows warm orange-pink like polished copper, long copper-coloured gloves and soft copper ballet flats.

Kari i sølvkjolen kari-solvkjole · Kari in the Silver Dress

Kari den andre søndagen, i en kjole sydd med sølvtråd over det hele, på en hest med sølvbrodert sal.

A slender young woman of about nineteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair in one loose braid woven with a silver ribbon. She wears a long, slim gown embroidered all over with silver thread that glitters like frost, a short silver-grey riding jacket and silver ankle boots, and carries a slim riding whip with a silver handle.

Kari i gullkjolen kari-gullkjole · Kari in the Gold Dress

Kari den tredje søndagen, i en kjole av nesten bare gull, besatt med klare steiner som glitrer som is, og med små sko av gull.

A slender young woman of about nineteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair flowing loose, held back by a slender gold band. She wears a long, full gown of gold cloth set all over with small clear stones that glitter like ice, and two small, pointed shoes of shining gold.

Den blågrå oksen oksen · the Blue-Grey Ox

En stor okse som alltid er blank og ren uansett vær, som kan snakke, har en matduk i venstre øre og slåss mot trollene i skogene av kobber, sølv og gull for Kari.

A huge, gentle ox, taller at the shoulder than a grown man, with a glossy, spotless blue-grey coat that stays clean and shining in any weather, a paler grey muzzle, big, soft dark-brown eyes with long lashes, two long, smooth cream-white horns curving upwards, large soft ears, a curly tuft of darker blue-grey hair between the horns, a long tail ending in a navy-blue tassel and dark grey hooves. Calm, kind and very strong.

Stemora stemora · the Stepmother

Kongens nye dronning, som smiler til alle og mener det med ingen, tar fra Kari mobilen og maten og betaler privatlegen for å si at hun bare blir frisk av oksekjøtt.

A tall, thin woman of about forty-five with a long, pinched face, a sharp pointed nose, narrow pale-green eyes, thin arched eyebrows, a small mouth fixed in a bright smile that never reaches her eyes, and jet-black hair scraped into a tight, sleek bun held by a spiky silver clip. She wears a stiff, high-necked slate-grey designer dress, a long black wool coat draped over her shoulders and many heavy silver rings, and holds a white handkerchief.

Stesøstera stesostera · the Stepsister

Dattera til stemora, akkurat så slem som Kari er snill. Hun får gullskoen på og blir pyntet til brud.

A gangly young woman of about twenty with a long, sour face, a pinched, turned-up nose, small squinting pale-green eyes, a pouting mouth and thin, straw-pale hair in two stiff braids that stick out sideways. She wears a frilly blouse the sour green of unripe gooseberries, covered in pink bows, a short pleated green skirt, white tights and pointed green shoes on very long, big feet.

Prinsen prinsen · the Prince

En ung, ugift prins med et ansikt for forsida av et ukeblad, som tømmer vaskevannet over oppvaskjenta og så ikke kan ta øynene fra den ukjente jenta i kirka.

A broad-shouldered young man of about twenty-five with a proud, stubborn, magazine-cover face, a strong jaw, a slightly hooked nose, bright blue eyes under straight fair brows and thick, wavy honey-blond hair swept back from his forehead and falling to his collar. He wears a slim dark-green wool suit over a heather-purple shirt with an open collar, a round gold pin on his lapel and polished black leather boots.

Mannen i berget mannen-i-berget · the Man from the Rock

En mørkkledd mann som kommer ut av bergveggen når Kari banker, med kjoler og hest til kirka og mørke, rolige øyne hun synes hun har sett før.

A small, sturdy man of no clear age with a broad, calm face, a big round nose, big, calm dark-brown eyes with long lashes and thick, short blue-grey hair with one curly tuft at the front. He wears a long charcoal wool coat buttoned to the neck, a dark knitted jumper, dark trousers and heavy black boots, and carries a small brass lantern that glows warm yellow.

Trollet med tre hoder trollet-med-tre-hoder · the Three-Headed Troll

Trollet som eier kobberskogen. Det har tre hoder, og alle tre er sinte når noen rører skogen.

A squat, pot-bellied troll about twice as tall as a man, with chalk-white, lumpy skin speckled with grey freckles and patches of moss, short bandy legs and long dangling arms. It has three bald, egg-shaped heads on three thick necks, each with a big red bulbous nose, small round orange eyes, one crooked tooth and tufts of stiff orange hair behind the ears. It wears huge, ragged brown canvas work trousers held up with rope, with a curved cow horn of salve hanging from the rope.

Trollet med ni hoder trollet-med-ni-hoder · the Nine-Headed Troll

Trollet som eier gullskogen, sterkere enn de to andre trollene til sammen. Hver gang oksen stanger i hjel et av hodene, blåser de andre liv i det igjen.

An enormous, pear-shaped troll as tall as a four-storey building, with lumpy, heather-pink skin, a huge round belly and short, stumpy arms and legs. Along its broad shoulders sit nine small round heads in a row, each with puffy cheeks, a tiny snub nose, small black eyes under bushy grey brows, big round ears and a shock of spiky grey hair. It wears an enormous faded brown tarpaulin tied round its middle with rope, with a curved cow horn of salve hanging from it.

Så fikk kongen krig med en annen konge. Det var den moderne sorten, som føres av advokater, og den holdt ham borte i et halvt år. Nå kunne stemora gjøre som hun ville. Først tok hun fra Kari mobilen, så tok hun maten. Hun slo også, men aldri der det ville synes. Til slutt fant hun ut at alt i slottet var for godt for Kari, og satte henne til å gjete kyrne.

Create the cover illustration for an illustrated book of modern fairy tales, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: Dusk on the Beach below the castle, under a huge, low orange moon. Lillekort stands on the sand at the water's edge in his big hoodie, feet apart, holding a scrap-looking sword whose blade flashes with light where its paper wrapping has slipped, gazing boldly out to sea, where a black ship is coming through the silver mist. Behind him, Princess Nora, in a long black coat, sits on the flat stone, and up in the old oak Sir Red peeks out between the leaves. Camera flashes glitter far up at the castle gate.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Lillekort: A small, bold boy only minutes old but already the size of a child of about six, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes, a determined little chin and a mop of golden curls. An oversized knitted beanie with blue-and-white stripes flops over one ear. He wears his big brothers' hand-me-downs: a huge, faded navy-blue hoodie with the sleeves pushed up, grey trousers a little too big for him, rolled at the ankles, and worn white trainers with holes in the toes.
- Princess Nora: A slim, lively princess of about nineteen with a round face, a pointed little chin, a small turned-up nose, big grey eyes, pale skin with pink cheeks and short, bouncy platinum-blonde curls held back by a slim gold hairband. She wears a simple, elegant emerald-green knee-length dress, a fine gold chain with one small pearl, black tights and black ankle boots.
- Sir Red: The head of the royal guards: a big, burly, barrel-chested man of about forty, a head taller than most men, with a broad, puffy face that easily turns bright red, a big bulbous nose, small shifty pale-blue eyes under bushy brows, curly red hair, a big, well-groomed fiery-red beard and a dazzling, camera-ready smile. He wears a long bright-red coat over a dark-blue guard's uniform with gold buttons, polished black boots and a white handkerchief in his breast pocket.

Setting:
- the Beach: A wide, pale sandy beach below the castle on the headland, curving along the open sea. A big, flat grey boulder lies at the water's edge, and at the top of the beach stands a huge, gnarled old oak with spreading branches and yellow-brown leaves. Beach grass grows on the low dunes, and a path with iron railings climbs to the dark stone castle with its glass extensions, towers and antennas.

Story world: Present-day Norway on the open coast. Lillekort is born in a cramped three-room flat with a wood stove in an old apartment block. The royal estate is an old castle of dark stone at the tip of a headland, rebuilt with glass and antennas, with towers, a gate, a park, a quay and a big old-fashioned kitchen with a wood-fired range; below it lies a wide sandy beach with a big old oak. While the princess is promised to the trolls, black mourning flags hang from the towers. The trolls come over the sea in black ships. Lillekort's sword looks like scrap wrapped in old newspaper until its blade catches the light. His ship folds up as small as a matchbox of shiny metal and unfolds, panel by panel, into a sea-going ship with lights in its hull. The princess's three secret garments are thin as foil.

This story's season, light and colours: Late autumn on the open coast: grey, blustery days, a dark-green sea with whitecaps and yellow birch leaves blowing across wet tarmac. The three Thursday evenings lie under a huge, low orange moon, with silver sea mist and the hard white glare of camera lights. The wedding hall glitters under its light panels. Under the sea: cold green gloom, rusty pipes and a sea-green light seeping from the rock.

Art style: Contemporary Scandinavian editorial illustration: flat, graphic shapes with subtle risograph grain and a little hand-drawn texture, clean confident lines and a limited palette of spot inks led by deep petrol blue, with fjord teal, lingonberry red, honey mustard, sage green, warm paper off-white and ink charcoal, like the pages of a risograph-printed book, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, in the cool, clear Nordic light of today. Present-day Norway: fjord towns, suburbs, farms with tractors, cabins, ferries, roadside petrol stations, offices and flats, grey rain and bright snow, with people in modern clothes such as rain jackets, knitted sweaters, hoodies, suits and work wear. The magic of the tale appears plainly in this everyday world: trolls, talking animals and enchantments look real and slightly absurd, drawn in the same flat style. Every character has their own face, build, age, hair and clothes exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Dry humour, careful composition with one focal point and plenty of negative space. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.
