Characters

Lillekort lillekort · Lillekort

Født i en trang leilighet og går ut i verden samme dag, en kvikk, fryktløs småtass som får tak i «umulige» gjenstander og bruker dem til å redde andre—uten å kreve æren.

A small, bold boy only minutes old but already the size of a child of about six, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes, a determined little chin and a mop of golden curls. An oversized knitted beanie with blue-and-white stripes flops over one ear. He wears his big brothers' hand-me-downs: a huge, faded navy-blue hoodie with the sleeves pushed up, grey trousers a little too big for him, rolled at the ankles, and worn white trainers with holes in the toes.

Lillekort i gullkledningen lillekort-gull · Lillekort in Gold

Lillekort i gulldrakten som prinsesse Nora trakk på ham mens han sov. Den er tynn som folie, og han skjuler den under hettegenseren helt til bryllupet.

The same small, bold boy, the size of a child of about six, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes, a determined little chin and a mop of golden curls under his oversized blue-and-white striped beanie. He now wears a shining garment of gold as thin as foil, which fits him like a second skin from neck to wrists and ankles and glows with its own warm light, with his worn white trainers still on his feet.

Kong Lavring kong-lavring · Lavring

Tvillingbroren som forsvinner ut i verden i motsatt retning, like Lillekort av utseende men mer stolt og brå—og ender som nøkkelen til en rettferdig løsning.

A small, bold boy only minutes old but already the size of a child of about six, with exactly the same round face, rosy cheeks, button nose, big cornflower-blue eyes and mop of golden curls as his twin brother, but with a cheeky, know-it-all grin. He wears an oversized red-and-white striped beanie, a far-too-big mustard-yellow puffer jacket with the sleeves rolled up, baggy grey jeans and big green rubber boots.

Kong Lavring i Lillekorts klær kong-lavring-gull · Lavring in Gold

Kong Lavring i klærne til tvillingbroren, så lik at prinsessene tror det er Lillekort som kommer.

The small twin dressed in his brother's clothes, so that nobody can tell the two apart: a bold boy the size of a child of about six, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes and a mop of golden curls under an oversized blue-and-white striped beanie, in a shining garment of gold as thin as foil that fits him like a second skin, and worn white trainers.

Prinsesse Nora prinsesse-nora · Princess Nora

Den yngste prinsessa, fanget i en moderne hoffverden av sorg og plikt, som finner mot til å avsløre sannheten når Lillekort gir henne en plan.

A slim, lively princess of about nineteen with a round face, a pointed little chin, a small turned-up nose, big grey eyes, pale skin with pink cheeks and short, bouncy platinum-blonde curls held back by a slim gold hairband. She wears a simple, elegant emerald-green knee-length dress, a fine gold chain with one small pearl, black tights and black ankle boots.

Den eldste prinsessa eldste-prinsessa · the Elder Princess

Kongens andre datter, som trollet tok med seg til berget på havbunnen. Der sitter hun og syr til Lillekort kommer, og hun er både størst og sterkest av de to søstrene.

A tall, strong, broad-shouldered young woman of about twenty-two, a head taller than her younger sister and quick on her feet, with a round face, a pointed chin, a small turned-up nose, big grey eyes, pink cheeks and thick platinum-blonde curls tumbling to her shoulders, held back with a string of pearls. She wears a long, faded coral-red knitted dress with little white shells sewn along the hem, a plaited silver cord belt and a silver thimble on one finger.

Ridder Rød ridder-rod · Sir Red

En selvutnevnt helt og mediefavoritt som spiller «beskytter» men gjemmer seg når det gjelder, og truer prinsessa til å gi ham æren.

The head of the royal guards: a big, burly, barrel-chested man of about forty, a head taller than most men, with a broad, puffy face that easily turns bright red, a big bulbous nose, small shifty pale-blue eyes under bushy brows, curly red hair, a big, well-groomed fiery-red beard and a dazzling, camera-ready smile. He wears a long bright-red coat over a dark-blue guard's uniform with gold buttons, polished black boots and a white handkerchief in his breast pocket.

Kjerringa med ett øye kjerringa · the One-Eyed Old Woman

Ei gammel, gammel, krokrygget kjerring med handlevogn og bare ett øye. Lillekort møter tre slike, og for å få øyet igjen gir de ham et sverd, et skip og kunsten å brygge.

A tiny, ancient woman, no taller than a child and bent so that her back curves like a hook, with a small, deeply wrinkled walnut face, a flat little nose, a wide toothless grin and only one eye: a single round, shiny sky-blue eye in the middle of her forehead that sits loose like a marble. Her thin white hair is in a tiny knot. She wears a faded lavender quilted coat, a brown knitted scarf and orthopaedic shoes, and pulls a battered tartan shopping trolley on two wheels.

Kongen kongen · the King

Kongen på det gamle slottet ytterst på neset. Han er glad i tradisjoner, har lovet bort den ene datteren til tre troll og har mistet den andre til et troll i havet.

A jolly, stocky king of about sixty who loves old traditions, with a big round belly, a broad, ruddy face made for laughing, a bulbous nose, crinkly brown eyes, bushy chestnut eyebrows, thick chestnut curls and a big, round, curly chestnut beard clipped short like a bush. He wears a rust-orange tweed jacket over a cream shirt, brown corduroy trousers and brown brogues and, every day, a small gold crown with seven points tipped with amber beads.

Kokken kokken · the Cook

Kokken på kongsgården, som Lillekort bærer ved og vann for, og som får fang på fang med bøyler av gull og sølv.

A sturdy, cheerful cook of about twenty-five with a broad, rosy, round face, merry dark-brown eyes, a snub nose dusted with flour and thick black hair wound into a bun under a white hairnet. Her sleeves are rolled up over strong arms. She wears a cornflower-blue chef's jacket, black-and-white checked trousers, a big white apron with soup stains and white clogs, and keeps a large wooden spoon tucked into her apron strings.

Trollet med fem hoder trollet-fem · the Five-Headed Troll

Det første av de tre trollene som prinsessa er lovet bort til. Det kommer over sjøen i et svart skip og vasser i land i en storm av skum og vind.

A huge, bloated sea troll about five times as tall as a man, with dusky purple-grey skin like an old mussel shell, crusted with barnacles and hung with dark seaweed, a great sagging belly, long dangling arms and flat, webbed feet. It has exactly five heads on five thick, wrinkled necks, each with a long drooping nose, small round yellow eyes and a tuft of shaggy grey hair. It wears a torn fishing net with orange plastic floats around its middle and carries a thick iron bar.

Trollet med ti hoder trollet-ti · the Ten-Headed Troll

Det andre trollet, dobbelt så stort som det første, med ti hoder og ei enda større jernstang.

An enormous sea troll about ten times as tall as a man, with rough slate-blue skin, knobbly and shiny like wet rock, a broad, square body, short thick legs and huge webbed feet. It has exactly ten round heads in two rows of five, one row above the other, each with a flat nose, big goggling green eyes, a wide frog mouth and a scraggly grey beard. It wears a torn black tarpaulin tied around its middle with rope and carries a huge iron bar.

Trollet med femten hoder trollet-femten · the Fifteen-Headed Troll

Det tredje og største trollet, med femten hoder og ei jernstang som får sanden til å sprute femten meter til værs.

The biggest sea troll of all, as tall as a hill, with dark peat-brown, lumpy skin like a bog, shaggy grey hair on its shoulders, a round belly and legs like old tree stumps. It has exactly fifteen heads stacked in a pyramid, five on its shoulders, then four, three, two and one on top, each with a round red nose, small blinking amber eyes and a shock of grey hair. It wears a huge patched tunic of old sailcloth tied with rope and carries a gigantic iron bar.

Havtrollet havtrollet · the Sea Troll

Et urgammelt troll som lever i en steinfestning på havbunnen og krever det umulige—til Lillekort vender trollfesten mot dem selv med et brygg som slår selv monsterkrefter ut.

A fat, hot-tempered troll about three times as tall as a man, with smooth, shiny turquoise skin like a wet fish, a barrel belly, short bowed legs and big flat webbed feet. He has one huge head with a gigantic, wrinkly, trumpet-shaped nose that is always sniffing, bulging pale-orange eyes, bristly orange eyebrows and a long tangle of brown kelp for hair and beard, crusted with salt. He wears baggy faded yellow oilskin trousers held up by a rope and a necklace of big shells.

Princess Nora, in her black coat, stands frozen at the water's edge. Lillekort, in his big hoodie, has just come running down the path and plants his feet in the sand. High in the oak, Sir Red hides among the leaves.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Five-Headed Troll: A huge, bloated sea troll about five times as tall as a man, with dusky purple-grey skin like an old mussel shell, crusted with barnacles and hung with dark seaweed, a great sagging belly, long dangling arms and flat, webbed feet. It has exactly five heads on five thick, wrinkled necks, each with a long drooping nose, small round yellow eyes and a tuft of shaggy grey hair. It wears a torn fishing net with orange plastic floats around its middle and carries a thick iron bar.
- Princess Nora: A slim, lively princess of about nineteen with a round face, a pointed little chin, a small turned-up nose, big grey eyes, pale skin with pink cheeks and short, bouncy platinum-blonde curls held back by a slim gold hairband. She wears a simple, elegant emerald-green knee-length dress, a fine gold chain with one small pearl, black tights and black ankle boots.
- Lillekort: A small, bold boy only minutes old but already the size of a child of about six, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes, a determined little chin and a mop of golden curls. An oversized knitted beanie with blue-and-white stripes flops over one ear. He wears his big brothers' hand-me-downs: a huge, faded navy-blue hoodie with the sleeves pushed up, grey trousers a little too big for him, rolled at the ankles, and worn white trainers with holes in the toes.
- Sir Red: The head of the royal guards: a big, burly, barrel-chested man of about forty, a head taller than most men, with a broad, puffy face that easily turns bright red, a big bulbous nose, small shifty pale-blue eyes under bushy brows, curly red hair, a big, well-groomed fiery-red beard and a dazzling, camera-ready smile. He wears a long bright-red coat over a dark-blue guard's uniform with gold buttons, polished black boots and a white handkerchief in his breast pocket.

Setting:
- the Beach: A wide, pale sandy beach below the castle on the headland, curving along the open sea. A big, flat grey boulder lies at the water's edge, and at the top of the beach stands a huge, gnarled old oak with spreading branches and yellow-brown leaves. Beach grass grows on the low dunes, and a path with iron railings climbs to the dark stone castle with its glass extensions, towers and antennas.

Story world: Present-day Norway on the open coast. Lillekort is born in a cramped three-room flat with a wood stove in an old apartment block. The royal estate is an old castle of dark stone at the tip of a headland, rebuilt with glass and antennas, with towers, a gate, a park, a quay and a big old-fashioned kitchen with a wood-fired range; below it lies a wide sandy beach with a big old oak. Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Fifteen-Headed Troll: The biggest sea troll of all, as tall as a hill, with dark peat-brown, lumpy skin like a bog, shaggy grey hair on its shoulders, a round belly and legs like old tree stumps. It has exactly fifteen heads stacked in a pyramid, five on its shoulders, then four, three, two and one on top, each with a round red nose, small blinking amber eyes and a shock of grey hair. It wears a huge patched tunic of old sailcloth tied with rope and carries a gigantic iron bar.
- Lillekort: A small, bold boy only minutes old but already the size of a child of about six, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes, a determined little chin and a mop of golden curls. He wears his big brothers' hand-me-downs: a huge, faded navy-blue hoodie with the sleeves pushed up, grey trousers a little too big for him, rolled at the ankles, and worn white trainers with holes in the toes.
- Princess Nora: A slim, lively princess of about nineteen with a round face, a pointed little chin, a small turned-up nose, big grey eyes, pale skin with pink cheeks and short, bouncy platinum-blonde curls held back by a slim gold hairband. She wears a simple, elegant emerald-green knee-length dress, a fine gold chain with one small pearl, black tights and black ankle boots.
- Sir Red: The head of the royal guards: a big, burly, barrel-chested man of about forty, a head taller than most men, with a broad, puffy face that easily turns bright red, a big bulbous nose, small shifty pale-blue eyes under bushy brows, curly red hair, a big, well-groomed fiery-red beard and a dazzling, camera-ready smile. - Lillekort in Gold: The same small, bold boy, the size of a child of about six, with a round face, rosy cheeks, a small button nose, big bright cornflower-blue eyes, a determined little chin and a mop of golden curls under his oversized blue-and-white striped beanie. - the Elder Princess: A tall, strong, broad-shouldered young woman of about twenty-two, a head taller than her younger sister and quick on her feet, with a round face, a pointed chin, a small turned-up nose, big grey eyes, pink cheeks and thick platinum-blonde curls tumbling to her shoulders, held back with a string of pearls. Alt: Fars datter går over ei endeløs eng med en blå kiste under armen, og småfuglene flyr rundt hodet hennes. Ved stien står ei tigerstripete ku og en nyklipt vær med ull rundt halsen, og bak dem står et epletre.

In the endless summer Meadow, the Girl walks along a faint path carrying the small blue chest under her arm and smiles up at the Little Birds fluttering round her head. Beside the path stand the brindled Cow with the wooden bowl on her horns and the Ram, freshly sheared, with a thick scarf of wool wound round his neck, both watching her kindly. Behind them stands an apple tree with straight, light branches.

Picture: In the endless summer Meadow, the Girl walks along a faint path carrying the small blue chest under her arm and smiles up at the Little Birds fluttering round her head. Beside the path stand the brindled Cow with the wooden bowl on her horns and the Ram, freshly sheared, with a thick scarf of wool wound round his neck, both watching her kindly. Behind them stands an apple tree with straight, light branches.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Girl: A slim, kind girl of about sixteen, a little small for her age, with a narrow, gentle face, big grey eyes, a small nose, pink cheeks and a quiet, steady look. Her light-brown wavy hair falls to her shoulders from under a blue cotton bandana knotted at the nape of her neck. She wears a plain blue pinafore dress over a white T-shirt and scuffed green rubber boots.
- the Little Birds: A small flock of exactly six identical tiny songbirds, blue tits no bigger than a plum: round and fluffy, with a sky-blue cap, wings and tail, a lemon-yellow breast, white cheeks with a thin black stripe through each eye, a short black beak, shiny black bead eyes and thin grey legs. They always stay close together and sing with their beaks wide open.
- the Cow: A big, gentle, plump cow with a brindled coat of dark brown and black streaks over reddish brown, long curved cream-coloured horns, big soft brown eyes with long lashes, a wet pink nose, a calm, friendly face and a swishing tail with a white tuft. Her udder is huge and round, and a wooden bowl hangs by a leather thong from her horns.
- the Ram: A big, round ram who is more wool than ram: his creamy-white wool is so long and thick that it trails behind him like a bridal veil. He has a black face, black legs, big curly golden-brown horns, sleepy half-closed amber eyes and a soft, silly smile, and a pair of wool shears hangs from one of his horns.

Setting:
- the Meadow: An endless summer meadow at the bottom of a well, with no houses, roads or power lines anywhere: tall, soft green grass full of clover, buttercups, harebells and bumblebees under a hazy sky. A faint path runs across it past an old-fashioned fence of woven brushwood twigs, like one in a folk museum, and an old apple tree with a long pole leaning against its trunk.

Story world: Present-day rural Norway. At home: a red house on a hillside, with a garden, an old stone well without a lid and an old plank outbuilding that was once a pigsty. The stepmother sells hand-spun yarn online. At the bottom of the well lies another world: an endless summer meadow with no houses or power lines, crossed by an old-fashioned fence of woven brushwood twigs, with an apple tree and a long pole by its trunk. Far across it lies a farm that looks too ordinary. The old woman lives there with her daughter, a younger copy of her with the same hooked nose. The sieve is a round wooden frame with a mesh bottom. The three small chests are gaudy like souvenirs, red, green and blue, with heavy old locks; three tiny crosses are scratched into the lock of the blue one.

This story's season, light and colours: Two worlds. At home: a warm June afternoon on a green hillside, with low sun on the old stone well, and later the dusk-lit living room. Below the well: an endless meadow in hazy, timeless summer light, full of flowers and bumblebees; the too-ordinary farm silent under a flat white sky; a dim cowshed. At the end, an old outbuilding glowing gold through every crack. Accents: the Girl's blue bandana and dress, a mustard-yellow hoodie, and the red, green and blue chests.

Characters

Fars datter fars-datter · the Girl

Stille og arbeidsom stedatter som møter urett med ro, løser umulige oppgaver med hjelp fra naturen, og velger riktig kiste uten å la seg blende.

A slim, kind girl of about sixteen, a little small for her age, with a narrow, gentle face, big grey eyes, a small nose, pink cheeks and a quiet, steady look. Her light-brown wavy hair falls to her shoulders from under a blue cotton bandana knotted at the nape of her neck. She wears a plain blue pinafore dress over a white T-shirt and scuffed green rubber boots.

Mors datter mors-datter · the Stepsister

Bortskjemt og aggressiv, tramper over alt som ber om omtanke, avviser hjelpen hun får, og velger den mest glorete kista—med katastrofale følger.

A sturdy, broad-shouldered girl of about sixteen with a broad, square face, a heavy jaw, full lips pushed out in a sulk, a wide flat nose, small dark eyes under heavy black eyebrows drawn together in a scowl, and a big, bushy cloud of black frizzy hair tied on top with a red scrunchie. She wears a pink T-shirt, light-wash jeans and chunky white trainers, with a phone in a glittery case sticking out of her back pocket.

Stemoren stemoren · the Stepmother

Kontrollerende og bitter voksen som favoriserer sin egen datter, skyver stedatteren ut av hjemmet og forsøker å gjøre belønning til noe hun kan stjele.

A short, stout, bossy woman of about forty-five with a big, doughy face, heavy cheeks, a small snub nose, small cold black eyes, a sour little mouth and frizzy black hair streaked with grey, bundled into a big messy knot on top of her head. She wears a dark-plum hand-knitted cardigan over a black linen dress, with a large round silver brooch at her collar, and always has her phone in her hand, ready to take pictures.

Den gamle kvinnen på gården den-gamle-kvinnen · the Old Woman

En kald, beregnende arbeidsgiver på en «for vanlig» og altfor stille gård, som setter folk på prøver og tilbyr tre kister som lønn—en test av karakter, ikke arbeid.

A big, heavy, barrel-shaped old woman, a head taller than a grown woman and twice as broad, with a wrinkled, sallow face, a very long, knobbly, hooked nose, one thick bushy grey eyebrow straight across her forehead, small squinting black eyes, a sour down-turned mouth and a wart on her chin. Her grey hair is pulled back tight. She wears a dark-red shawl over a charcoal-grey cardigan, a long dark skirt and huge black rubber clogs, and a tufted cow's tail peeks out below the skirt.

Småfuglene smafuglene · the Little Birds

En liten fugleflokk som hvisker konkrete råd ved brønner og fjøs, og fungerer som historiens samvittighet: de hjelper den som lytter og vender seg bort fra den som slår.

A small flock of exactly six identical tiny songbirds, blue tits no bigger than a plum: round and fluffy, with a sky-blue cap, wings and tail, a lemon-yellow breast, white cheeks with a thin black stripe through each eye, a short black beak, shiny black bead eyes and thin grey legs. They always stay close together and sing with their beaks wide open.

Kua kua · the Cow

Ei tigerstripete ku på enga med ei trebolle på hornene. Hun vil bli melket, og siden gjemmer hun Fars datter under juret sitt.

A big, gentle, plump cow with a brindled coat of dark brown and black streaks over reddish brown, long curved cream-coloured horns, big soft brown eyes with long lashes, a wet pink nose, a calm, friendly face and a swishing tail with a white tuft. Her udder is huge and round, and a wooden bowl hangs by a leather thong from her horns.

Væren vaeren · the Ram

En vær som er mer ull enn vær. Han vil bli klipt, og siden gjemmer han Fars datter under ullskjerfet hun surret rundt halsen hans.

A big, round ram who is more wool than ram: his creamy-white wool is so long and thick that it trails behind him like a bridal veil. He has a black face, black legs, big curly golden-brown horns, sleepy half-closed amber eyes and a soft, silly smile, and a pair of wool shears hangs from one of his horns.

Story world: Present-day rural Norway. At home: a red house on a hillside, with a garden, an old stone well without a lid and an old plank outbuilding that was once a pigsty. The stepmother sells hand-spun yarn online. At the bottom of the well lies another world: an endless summer meadow with no houses or power lines, crossed by an old-fashioned fence of woven brushwood twigs, with an apple tree and a long pole by its trunk. Far across it lies a farm that looks too ordinary. The old woman lives there with her daughter, a younger copy of her with the same hooked nose. The sieve is a round wooden frame with a mesh bottom. The three small chests are gaudy like souvenirs, red, green and blue, with heavy old locks; three tiny crosses are scratched into the lock of the blue one.

At the end, an old outbuilding glowing gold through every crack. Accents: the Girl's blue bandana and dress, a mustard-yellow hoodie, and the red, green and blue chests.

En gammel kvinne åpnet døra før Fars datter rakk å banke. Hun hadde grått hår, strammet bakover, og et mørkerødt sjal over skuldrene. Bak henne i gangen sto dattera hennes og stirret uten å blunke.

En gammel kvinne åpnet døra før Fars datter rakk å banke.

Alt: Fars datter står foran et helt vanlig hvitt våningshus med hånden løftet for å banke, men døra er allerede åpen. Der står en stor, gammel kvinne med mørkerødt sjal, og bak henne stirrer dattera hennes.

The Too-Ordinary Farm under a flat white sky, silent, with nobody about and only small birds on the barn roof. Behind her in the dim hallway, her daughter stares without blinking.

Picture: The Too-Ordinary Farm under a flat white sky, silent, with nobody about and only small birds on the barn roof. Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Girl: A slim, kind girl of about sixteen, a little small for her age, with a narrow, gentle face, big grey eyes, a small nose, pink cheeks and a quiet, steady look. Her light-brown wavy hair falls to her shoulders from under a blue cotton bandana knotted at the nape of her neck. She wears a plain blue pinafore dress over a white T-shirt and scuffed green rubber boots.
- the Old Woman: A big, heavy, barrel-shaped old woman, a head taller than a grown woman and twice as broad, with a wrinkled, sallow face, a very long, knobbly, hooked nose, one thick bushy grey eyebrow straight across her forehead, small squinting black eyes, a sour down-turned mouth and a wart on her chin. Her grey hair is pulled back tight. She wears a dark-red shawl over a charcoal-grey cardigan, a long dark skirt and huge black rubber clogs, and a tufted cow's tail peeks out below the skirt.

Setting:
- the Too-Ordinary Farm: A farm that looks a little too ordinary, under a flat white sky: a white two-storey farmhouse, a red barn, a bare flagpole with no flag, a gravel yard with an old stone well and a big wooden tub beside it, and no tractor, no dog, no car and nobody about. Everything is neat and silent.

Story world: Present-day rural Norway. At home: a red house on a hillside, with a garden, an old stone well without a lid and an old plank outbuilding that was once a pigsty. The stepmother sells hand-spun yarn online. At the bottom of the well lies another world: an endless summer meadow with no houses or power lines, crossed by an old-fashioned fence of woven brushwood twigs, with an apple tree and a long pole by its trunk. Far across it lies a farm that looks too ordinary. The old woman lives there with her daughter, a younger copy of her with the same hooked nose. The sieve is a round wooden frame with a mesh bottom. The three small chests are gaudy like souvenirs, red, green and blue, with heavy old locks; three tiny crosses are scratched into the lock of the blue one.

This story's season, light and colours: Two worlds. At home: a warm June afternoon on a green hillside, with low sun on the old stone well, and later the dusk-lit living room. Below the well: an endless meadow in hazy, timeless summer light, full of flowers and bumblebees; the too-ordinary farm silent under a flat white sky; a dim cowshed. At the end, an old outbuilding glowing gold through every crack. Accents: the Girl's blue bandana and dress, a mustard-yellow hoodie, and the red, green and blue chests.

#07 · fars-datter, smafuglene
modern · after paragraph 41
Fars datter visste mye om ull. Hun visste at svart ull ikke blir hvit, uansett hva man vasker den i. Hun sa ingenting. Hun tok ulla med til brønnen, og fuglene sang at hun skulle legge den i den store balja som sto der. Da hun løftet den opp igjen, var den hvit som nysnø.

Da hun løftet den opp igjen, var den hvit som nysnø.

Alt: Ved brønnen på gården løfter Fars datter ulla opp av ei stor balje. Vannet er svart, men ulla er blitt hvit som nysnø. På kanten av balja sitter småfuglene og synger.

Characters

Mestertyven (yngstesønnen) mestertyven · the Master Thief

En ressurssterk, blakk unggutt som lærer seg kriminell finesse for å overleve, men som også har en egen moral og vil ut av livet som tyv.

A wiry, nimble young man of about twenty-two with a sharp-featured, clever face, a pointed chin, quick dark-brown eyes under arched eyebrows, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache. Short curly black hair pokes out from under a small dark-grey wool flat cap worn tilted over one eye. He wears a long, worn bottle-green parka with deep pockets over a cream hoodie, a thin red scarf, charcoal jeans and black leather boots.

Mestertyven i dress mestertyven-dress · the Suited Son

Mestertyven i en dress han fant blant tingene til ranerne, sydd til en mann som er vant til at folk reiser seg når han kommer inn i et rom. Slik kjører han hjem til faren som en annen storkar.

The master thief dressed like a very rich man: the same wiry young man of about twenty-two with a sharp-featured, clever face, a pointed chin, a sly lopsided grin, a thin black moustache and short curly black hair, now slicked back. He wears a made-to-measure midnight-blue three-piece suit with a white pocket square, a pale-pink shirt, a bottle-green silk tie, a heavy gold watch, oxblood loafers and a long camel overcoat.

Mestertyven i filler mestertyven-fillegutt · the Scruffy Lad

Mestertyven i utslitte klær og en hullete jakke, så elendig og lurvete at det er helt ynkelig. Ingen ser på en som ser sånn ut. I sekken har han tre levende harer.

The master thief disguised as a pitiful down-and-out: the same wiry young man with a sharp-featured, clever face, a pointed chin, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache, his cheeks smudged with dirt and his curly black hair uncombed. He wears a filthy brown work jacket full of holes over a stained grey hoodie, baggy ripped tracksuit bottoms and split, muddy trainers, and carries a big lumpy sack over one shoulder.

Mestertyven som engel mestertyven-engel · the Pretend Angel

Mestertyven med et stort, hvitt laken over seg og de to gåsevingene faren feide aske med på ryggen. Oppe i lønnetreet forkynner han presten at han skal tas opp levende til Guds rike.

The master thief disguised as an angel: the same wiry young man with a sharp-featured, clever face, a pointed chin, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache. A big white bedsheet is draped over his head and body like a long hooded robe, leaving his face free, and two old grey-and-white goose wings, the kind used for sweeping ash from a stove, are tied onto his back with string, a little crooked. His bare feet peek out below the sheet.

Mestertyven som kjerring mestertyven-kjerring · the Beggar Crone

Mestertyven i et fillete skjørt og en strikkejakke lånt av ei gammel kone, med stokk i handa og pose over skulderen. Hun fryser så fælt, og hun har to lommelerker med seg.

The master thief disguised as a crooked old beggar woman: a stooped, limping figure leaning on a wooden walking cane, with a cloth bag over one shoulder. A faded floral headscarf is tied over a tangled grey wig, but a thin black moustache and a sly grin peek out underneath. He wears a baggy, bobbly grey knitted cardigan, a ragged brown skirt that is too short, laddered thick tights and muddy rubber boots.

Mestertyven med geiteskjegg mestertyven-tonnemann · the Barrel Man

Mestertyven i filler, med sot i ansiktet, parykk og et stort skjegg av geitehår, så ingen kan kjenne ham igjen. Han skal i bryllup med ei tønne hjemmebrygg og må holde fingeren i hullet i tønna.

The master thief disguised as a wretched old carter, unrecognisable: his face smeared with soot, a shaggy grey wig and a huge, bushy false beard of grey-white goat hair reaching down to his belt, with only his sly, narrow dark eyes showing. He wears a squashed black knitted hat, a ragged, oil-stained brown coat tied with orange baler twine, patched trousers and cracked rubber boots.

Den gamle dama i basen den-gamle-dama · the Old Lady

En sliten eldre kvinne som holder til i en ombygd industrilåve og lever tett på en gjeng hun frykter, men som likevel gir gutten en sjanse til å overleve natta.

A short, round old woman of about seventy with red apple cheeks, a button nose, shrewd twinkling blue eyes, deep laugh lines and wisps of white hair escaping from a red-and-white checked headscarf knotted at the back of her neck. She wears a worn, faded sunflower-yellow hoodie over a long flowered nightgown, thick wool socks and tartan felt slippers, with a big wooden ladle sticking out of the hoodie's front pocket.

Faren faren · the Father

En blakk far som leier den gamle husmannsplassen nedenfor storgården og har knapt til husleia. Han blir drevet opp alleen for å be stormannen om dattera på vegne av sønnen.

A thin, timid man of about sixty-five with a long, droopy, worried face, big sad grey eyes under bushy brows, a red-tipped nose, sunken cheeks with grey stubble and thin grey hair sticking up in tufts. He wears a threadbare mouse-brown cardigan with leather elbow patches over a washed-out grey T-shirt, baggy corduroy trousers and old rubber clogs, and wraps a worn grey-and-blue striped wool blanket round his shoulders like a shawl.

Bonden med oksene bonden · the Farmer

En bonde med en gammel pickup og dyrehenger som skal kjøre oksene til slakteriet uten at kona får vite det, og som blir lurt tre ganger på den samme grusveien.

A big, broad, soft-hearted farmer of about forty with a round, weathered face, a bulbous red nose, small worried blue eyes, large ears and a short, curly light-brown beard. He wears a battered brown waxed cap, a dark-green rain jacket over a woolly sheepskin-lined vest and a blue work shirt, brown work trousers and muddy green rubber boots.

Stormannen stormannen · the Tycoon

En lokal rikmann med makt og prestisje som setter stadig mer ydmykende prøver for å avsløre mestertyven, men ender med å bli lurt på egne premisser.

A stout, self-important man of about fifty-five with a huge round belly, a pink double chin, rosy jowls, small twinkling eyes, a snub nose, a neat grey moustache waxed into two curly tips and grey hair curling over his ears. He wears a tobacco-brown tweed jacket over a canary-yellow knitted waistcoat stretched tight across his belly, a pale-blue shirt, a gold watch, grey trousers and shiny brown brogues.

Stormannens datter stormannens-datter · the Tycoon's Daughter

Smart og snill, med sterk integritet; hun lar seg ikke blende av triks, men krever at mestertyven kan lære å gi tilbake.

A clever young woman of about twenty-two with a heart-shaped face, a dimple in one cheek, lively grey-green eyes that always seem to be laughing, a small straight nose and nut-brown hair in two braids pinned into round buns over her ears. She wears an apricot-coloured wool jumper with a white shirt collar showing, dark jeans and white trainers, with a small enamel lily-of-the-valley pin on the jumper.

Presten presten · the Vicar

Selvsikker og moraliserende, overbevist om at han ikke kan lures—helt til mestertyven bruker forkledning og religiøst språk mot ham.

A tall, stiff, very proud vicar of about fifty with a long thin face, a long pointed nose held high, raised eyebrows, a small pursed mouth and a long, pointed sandy-grey beard. He wears a black clerical shirt with a white collar tab under a long black wool coat, dark trousers and polished black shoes, and clasps a small black hymn book to his chest.

Nearby lie a playground with a new brushed-steel drinking fountain that only gives water for a code from the park app, a park with a barbecue area and a small wooden kiosk selling ice cream and barbecue charcoal, and a shopping centre with glass doors, an escalator, a goldsmith's, a shoe-repair booth and a hardware shop. Across the ring road lies a farm with a pig behind the barn and a field being harvested.

This story's season, light and colours: Early September on a clear, bright Saturday: high blue sky, crisp sunlight and long afternoon shadows, hazel bushes still green with the first yellow leaves, red rowan berries, golden stubble and dust over the fields, and pastel blocks of flats glowing in the sun. Accents: the Rooster's scarlet comb, the Kiosk Boy's bottle-green jacket and gleaming brushed steel.

Hun gikk de tolv kilometerne hjem.

On the county road at dusk, the Feathered Wife trudges home in her green rubber boots, a huge black-feathered figure with her arms held out from her sides, feathers drifting off her into the air. A single passing car lights her up with its headlights. Far ahead, at the end of the road, the Smallholding sits under the first stars.

A single passing car lights her up with its headlights. Far ahead, at the end of the road, the Smallholding sits under the first stars.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Feathered Wife: The Wife after the Butcher's prank: the same round woman of about forty-five with a long ski-jump nose, big round amazed blue eyes and two long straw-yellow plaits, in her padded jacket, jumper, work trousers and green rubber boots, but now painted black with roofing tar from her hair down to her boots and covered all over with fluffy white, grey and brown feathers and down, so that she looks like a huge, ruffled black bird.

Setting:
- the Smallholding: A small, run-down smallholding on a gentle slope: a white wooden farmhouse with peeling paint and a front porch, a red barn with a single lamp over the barn door, a little old storehouse on stone legs with a steep roof, an old red tractor, and one brown field ringed by a wire fence, with bare birches and grey snowbanks melting along the road.

Story world: Present-day rural eastern Norway, just before the spring ploughing. The Farmer and the Wife have a small, run-down smallholding with one brown field, an old tractor and a car that failed its inspection. A county road leads twelve kilometres to a small town, where the Butcher has a little shop with a back room of steel shelves and plastic crates and a cold room behind a shiny steel door. Along the roads further off stand a brand-new white house with no windows, a house whose kitchen is full of knitting, and an old farm at the far end of a valley with a shed by the barn. The widow's horse is a blue-grey dappled horse with a black mane and tail, harnessed to a small two-wheeled cart; Per the Third's plough horse is a stocky dark-brown Døle horse.

This story's season, light and colours: A dry, cold spring just before the ploughing: pale sunshine under a high, thin sky, brown fields and grey road dust, dirty snowbanks melting at the roadsides, birches with bare purple twigs and the first mouse-ear leaves, dark spruce and dry heather on the hills, and evenings under yellow yard lamps. At the end, a grey rain shower hanging over the ridge.

Characters

Kona kona · the Wife

Stolt og sta småbrukerkone som skal skaffe såkorn, men blir lurt i byen, drikker seg sanseløs og våkner så full av tjære og fjær at hun ikke lenger er sikker på at hun er seg.

A cheerful, dreamy smallholder's wife of about forty-five, a little round, with a long ski-jump nose, big round blue eyes that always look amazed, rosy cheeks, a pleased little smile and two long, thin straw-yellow plaits tied at the ends with red hair ties. She wears a rust-orange padded jacket over a black knitted jumper with a red zigzag band, dark work trousers and green rubber boots.

Kona, full av tjære og fjær kona-med-fjaer · the Feathered Wife

Kona etter slakterens puss: svart av taktjære og full av fjær og dun fra håret og ned til gummistøvlene, så speilbildet ser ut som en stor, svart fugl.

The Wife after the Butcher's prank: the same round woman of about forty-five with a long ski-jump nose, big round amazed blue eyes and two long straw-yellow plaits, in her padded jacket, jumper, work trousers and green rubber boots, but now painted black with roofing tar from her hair down to her boots and covered all over with fluffy white, grey and brown feathers and down, so that she looks like a huge, ruffled black bird.

Mannen mannen · the Farmer

Utslitt småbruker uten såkorn som går hjemmefra med verktøybelte og spade, og som ikke vil komme tilbake før han har truffet tre kjerringer som er like gale.

A lean, wiry smallholder of about forty-five with a narrow, clever face, a long straight nose, lively dark eyes with laugh crinkles, a patient half-smile, a short, neat black beard and cropped black hair. He wears a small black knitted cap with a turned-up brim, a faded cornflower-blue work jacket with big pockets, grey work trousers with a tool belt holding a folding ruler, and worn brown boots.

Slakteren slakteren · the Butcher

En glatt, utnyttende kjøttforhandler i en småby som lokker kona inn på bakrommet, skjenker henne full og gjør henne til en «fugl» med tjære og fjær for å ydmyke og forvirre henne.

A huge, barrel-chested butcher of about fifty with a round, shiny red face, a bulbous nose, twinkling little black eyes, bushy black eyebrows, a sly grin and a big, round, bushy black beard. He wears a small white cap, a red T-shirt with thick arms bulging from the sleeves, a long white apron with blue stripes and white rubber clogs, and he always has a string of sausages slung over one shoulder.

Kona med dørslaget kona-med-dorslaget · the Colander Woman

Ei fremmed kvinne i et nybygd hus langs veien, som prøver å bære sola inn i et dørslag fordi byggefirmaet glemte vinduene.

A tiny, quick, bird-like woman of about thirty with a small round face, a pointed chin, bright eager green eyes, rosy cheeks and a high, swinging red ponytail tied with a sunflower-yellow scrunchie. She wears an apricot-orange T-shirt under a white apron, jeans and red trainers, and she always carries a big, shiny steel colander full of little holes.

Enka etter Per nummer to enka · the Widow

Godtroende kvinne som forveksler Ringerike med «Himmerike» og sender klær, kontanter og hest av gårde til sin avdøde favorittmann, overbevist om at han trenger det der oppe.

A tall, big, well-fed farm woman of about sixty-five with a large round face, a double chin, pink cheeks, a big mouth always open to talk, bright little inquisitive eyes and tight iron-grey ringlets. She wears a wine-red dress under a long green knitted cardigan, a white apron and fleece-lined slippers.

Per nummer tre per · Per the Third

Enkas tredje mann, en gretten bonde som pløyer med hest og setter etter mannen fra Ringerike, men blir lurt til å ligge i lyngen og stirre opp i skyene.

A tall, heavy, grumpy farmer of about fifty-five with a long, sour face, a drooping lower lip, a big red nose, deep frown lines, bristly black eyebrows and a short, stiff iron-grey beard like a doormat. He wears a floppy black knitted hat, a patched brown work jacket over a rust-red flannel shirt, work trousers and tall muddy rubber boots.

From the dark gap under the bed, the Miller's Lad peers out at the feathers, holding his breath. Through the glass wall, the dark valley and the river lie far below.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Miller's Lad: A sturdy, broad-shouldered young man of about nineteen with a round, open, honest face, a button nose, friendly pale-blue eyes, a wide, warm grin and short, tight strawberry-blond curls. He wears a faded dove-grey baseball cap with a scarlet brim, a white T-shirt under an open oatmeal canvas work jacket, faded jeans and scuffed brown work boots.
- the Dragon: An ancient, heavy, pot-bellied dragon about twice as tall as a man, only just able to squeeze through a wide door, who walks upright on short, thick hind legs with big blunt claws. He has bumpy plum-purple scales dulled with age, a pale lavender belly, small leathery wings far too small for him, a long snout with round nostrils trailing smoke, big heavy-lidded amber eyes and a row of rust-orange spikes down his back. His long tail ends in exactly three long, shining golden feathers.

Setting:
- the Glass Hall: A vast, cold room inside a fortress-like house of grey concrete and dark glass built into a mountainside. One wall is dark glass looking out over a river valley, the others are raw grey concrete, and the polished black stone floor shines like a mirror. An enormous low bed with charcoal-grey covers and a dark gap beneath it stands at the far end, with a long grey sofa by the glass wall, a steel dining table, steel drawers and an old sword with a worn hilt on the concrete.

Story world: Present-day Norway, in a long inland valley where Rich Per owns half of everything. Just below his big modern house, an old stone mill house stands by a fast river; a couple of dozen kilometres downstream is a second old mill with a wooden waterwheel under the floor. The chest is a small, polished oak box with a heavy brass lock, its seams sealed with tar. Per's letter is a sealed white envelope. The thieves' hideout is a shabby smallholding deep in a spruce forest, and the young couple's smallholding lies up under a bare ridge. Far away runs a great, wide river with no bridge, and above it a fortress-like house of grey concrete and dark glass is built into the mountain. The three feathers are long, shining golden feathers.

This story's season, light and colours: A raw, grey November: low cloud and fog along the rivers, wet asphalt and gravel, black spruce, the last yellow birch leaves plastered to the ground, and dusk by four in the afternoon with orange street lights and warm lit windows. Characters

Møllergutten mollergutten · the Miller's Lad

Gutten som ble solgt som nyfødt og satt ut på elva i ei tjæret kiste, og som vokser opp på kverna lenger ned til en rolig, sterk ung mann som snur alle fellene til lykke.

A sturdy, broad-shouldered young man of about nineteen with a round, open, honest face, a button nose, friendly pale-blue eyes, a wide, warm grin and short, tight strawberry-blond curls. He wears a faded dove-grey baseball cap with a scarlet brim, a white T-shirt under an open oatmeal canvas work jacket, faded jeans and scuffed brown work boots.

Rike-Per rike-per · Rich Per

En kald og beregnende forretningsmann som eier halve dalen, behandler folk som eiendeler og prøver å kjøpe seg ut av spådommen, helt til grådigheten sender ham ut i elva.

A tall, bony businessman of about sixty with a long, horsey face, a jutting chin, a sharp hooked nose, small, darting, greedy grey eyes, a thin mouth, long bushy salt-and-pepper sideburns and slicked-back black hair streaked with grey, with a sharp widow's peak. He wears an expensive long wine-red wool overcoat over a charcoal suit, a green-and-gold striped silk tie, polished black shoes, a heavy gold signet ring and a chunky gold watch.

Pers datter pers-datter · Per's Daughter

Oppvokst under farens kontroll og giftet bort i all hast etter et forfalsket brev, men det er hun selv som sier ja, og ekteskapet blir veien ut av farens grep.

A tall, willowy young woman of about twenty-three with a long neck, a narrow face with a delicate chin, a small straight nose, soft brown eyes under pale brows, pink cheeks and a calm, direct gaze. Her thick auburn hair hangs in one long plait down her back, tied with a white band. She wears a midnight-blue wool jumper with a red-and-white knitted band at the hem and cuffs, dark jeans, brown leather boots and a small round silver pendant.

Laksekongens datter laksekongens-datter · the Salmon King's Daughter

Tatt av Dragen av Dybenfart for mange år siden og holdt fanget i et hus av glass og stål, gir hun møllergutten styrkedrikken og lurer dragen til å røpe svarene.

A small, quick-witted young woman of about twenty-four, very pale from years indoors, with a round face, a pointed little chin, a small straight nose, bright dark eyes that miss nothing and a wry, lopsided smile. Her dark-brown hair is cut short in a cap of springy curls, held back by a thin silver hairband set with one pearl. She wears a long, expensive turquoise silk dress with wide sleeves and soft grey slippers.

Dragen av Dybenfart dragen · the Dragon

En eldgammel drage som bor i et prisbelønt hus av betong og mørkt glass, bygd inn i fjellet. Han vil ha nattero, og den som har de tre fjærene fra halen hans, kan få hva han vil.

An ancient, heavy, pot-bellied dragon about twice as tall as a man, only just able to squeeze through a wide door, who walks upright on short, thick hind legs with big blunt claws. He has bumpy plum-purple scales dulled with age, a pale lavender belly, small leathery wings far too small for him, a long snout with round nostrils trailing smoke, big heavy-lidded amber eyes and a row of rust-orange spikes down his back. His long tail ends in exactly three long, shining golden feathers.

Fergemannen fergemannen · the Ferryman

En gammel, krokrygget mann som bærer folk over den brede elva på ryggen, dømt til å gjøre det til noen avløser ham.

A small, wiry, very old man, bent almost double with a back as crooked as a fish hook, yet strong as an ox. He has a wrinkled nut-brown face, a sharp beak of a nose, bright little black eyes under bushy snow-white eyebrows, a toothless grin, no beard, and thin white hair tied at the back in a stubby pigtail. He wears a battered straw hat, a faded sea-green anorak with patched elbows and grey work trousers rolled up above the knee, and goes barefoot.

The Ferryman stands in the current beside him and looks at him with a face like stone. On the near bank behind them, two big lorries, three trailers and a huge cool bag wait by the water's edge.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Rich Per: A tall, bony businessman of about sixty with a long, horsey face, a jutting chin, a sharp hooked nose, small, darting, greedy grey eyes, a thin mouth, long bushy salt-and-pepper sideburns and slicked-back black hair streaked with grey, with a sharp widow's peak. He wears an expensive long wine-red wool overcoat over a charcoal suit, a green-and-gold striped silk tie, polished black shoes, a heavy gold signet ring and a chunky gold watch.
- the Ferryman: A small, wiry, very old man, bent almost double with a back as crooked as a fish hook, yet strong as an ox. He has a wrinkled nut-brown face, a sharp beak of a nose, bright little black eyes under bushy snow-white eyebrows, a toothless grin, no beard, and thin white hair tied at the back in a stubby pigtail. He wears a battered straw hat, a faded sea-green anorak with patched elbows and grey work trousers rolled up above the knee, and goes barefoot.

Story world: Present-day Norway, in a long inland valley where Rich Per owns half of everything. Just below his big modern house, an old stone mill house stands by a fast river; a couple of dozen kilometres downstream is a second old mill with a wooden waterwheel under the floor. The chest is a small, polished oak box with a heavy brass lock, its seams sealed with tar. Per's letter is a sealed white envelope. The thieves' hideout is a shabby smallholding deep in a spruce forest, and the young couple's smallholding lies up under a bare ridge. Far away runs a great, wide river with no bridge, and above it a fortress-like house of grey concrete and dark glass is built into the mountain. The three feathers are long, shining golden feathers.

This story's season, light and colours: A raw, grey November: low cloud and fog along the rivers, wet asphalt and gravel, black spruce, the last yellow birch leaves plastered to the ground, and dusk by four in the afternoon with orange street lights and warm lit windows. In the concrete house: cold blue-white light, black glass and the glint of gold.

Smeden som de ikke turte slippe inn i helvete smehel · 12/12 pictures

Smeden og Fanden, som har kommet for å hente ham.

Alt: Smeden lener seg på slegga og smiler lurt. Ved siden av står en liten, rød djevel i lang, svart frakk med armene i kors. Bak dem henger pæretreet fullt av gule pærer.

In the gravel yard of the Workshop on a hot summer evening, the Smith leans on his big sledgehammer with a sly, twinkling grin, while the Devil, in his long black coat and shoes far too fine for the gravel, stands beside him with his arms crossed, tapping one foot impatiently and glaring up at him. Picture: In the gravel yard of the Workshop on a hot summer evening, the Smith leans on his big sledgehammer with a sly, twinkling grin, while the Devil, in his long black coat and shoes far too fine for the gravel, stands beside him with his arms crossed, tapping one foot impatiently and glaring up at him. Behind them, the old pear tree hangs heavy with yellow pears in the low sun.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Smith: A tall, long-legged blacksmith and farrier of about forty with a broad barrel chest and thick, strong forearms, a long, cocky face with a jutting chin, a big bumpy nose, twinkling hazel eyes, a chestnut-brown handlebar moustache curled up at both ends and short chestnut hair that sticks straight up like a brush. He wears a charcoal work T-shirt, a long scorched brown leather apron, dark-blue work trousers with knee pads, steel-toed black boots and a red bandana knotted round his neck.
- the Devil: A short, pot-bellied devil no taller than a boy of ten, with shiny tomato-red skin, a round face with a button nose, big goggly amber eyes, pointy ears, a long, pointed black goatee, two big black ram's horns curling out of his forehead and a very long, thin tail with an arrow-shaped tip. He wears a long black overcoat, a soot-black waistcoat with shiny brass buttons stretched over his belly and polished black shoes far too fine for gravel. Vain and silly rather than frightening.

Setting:
- the Yard: Outside the workshop: a long, dark-red steel-clad building with wide sliding doors and a roof vent, a gravel yard with a horse trailer, an old pear tree heavy with yellow pears against the side wall and a small white house next door. Beyond a low fence runs a county road with a guard rail, a grassy ditch full of cow parsley and summer fields.

Story world: Present-day Norway, a farming valley in summer. The Smith is the national champion farrier. His workshop is a long, dark-red steel-clad building by a county road, with a gravel yard for horse trailers, an old pear tree heavy with yellow pears against the side wall and his old mother's small white house next door. Inside are a coal forge with an electric fan and a big anvil, and in the break room a worn armchair patched with grey gaffer tape on one armrest. The steel-wire bag is a small, round coin purse of braided silver-grey steel wire with a snap clasp. Far along the road, the way forks: one road climbs into white clouds to a tall, pale gate; the other drops into a smoky gully to a tall black steel gate with an intercom and nine locks.

This story's season, light and colours: A hot, bright Norwegian summer: dusty gravel, yellow fields and green verges, cow parsley in the ditches and ripe yellow pears in the low evening sun. Inside the workshop: charcoal greys lit by the orange forge and white sparks. At the end, the gate of Heaven glows pale gold in white cloud, and the gate of Hell stands in plum-grey smoke.

Characters

Smeden smeden · the Smith

En selvsikker, sotete verkstedeier med et skryte-skilt over porten og en djevelkontrakt i skuffen; smart nok til å lure Fanden, men dumdristig nok til å etterligne mirakler han ikke forstår.

A tall, long-legged blacksmith and farrier of about forty with a broad barrel chest and thick, strong forearms, a long, cocky face with a jutting chin, a big bumpy nose, twinkling hazel eyes, a chestnut-brown handlebar moustache curled up at both ends and short chestnut hair that sticks straight up like a brush. He wears a charcoal work T-shirt, a long scorched brown leather apron, dark-blue work trousers with knee pads, steel-toed black boots and a red bandana knotted round his neck.

Vår Herre var-herre · Our Lord

En rolig vandrer som avslører ekte mesterskap ved å sko en hest og gjøre en gammel kvinne ung igjen, og som tilbyr smeden tre ønsker som blir brukt på list, ikke nåde.

A calm, slim man of about forty-five with an upright bearing, an oval face, a straight nose, warm dark-brown eyes with smile lines, long, curly dark-brown hair with a few silver threads falling to his shoulders and a short, neat dark-brown beard. He wears a loose, light linen shirt, pale linen trousers and worn leather sandals, and carries a slate-grey canvas sack over his shoulder and a plain wooden staff. No halo.

Sankt Peter sankt-peter · Saint Peter

Følgesvennen som ser gjennom smedens dumme ønsker og senere står ved himmelporten og bare åpner den på gløtt.

A tall, broad-shouldered old fisherman of about seventy with a weathered, ruddy face, a big round nose, pale blue eyes under bushy grey eyebrows and a thick, curly grey beard. He wears a navy-blue fisherman's cap with a short peak, a worn rust-brown canvas jacket over a grey fleece, dark trousers and sturdy hiking boots, and carries a sack and a wooden staff. A big, old iron key hangs from a leather cord at his belt. No halo.

Fanden fanden · the Devil

Kontraktsbundet innkrever som lar seg lokke av bekvemmelighet og stolthet, og blir fanget i pæretreet, i lenestolen på pauserommet og til slutt i smedens lille ståltrådveske.

A short, pot-bellied devil no taller than a boy of ten, with shiny tomato-red skin, a round face with a button nose, big goggly amber eyes, pointy ears, a long, pointed black goatee, two big black ram's horns curling out of his forehead and a very long, thin tail with an arrow-shaped tip. He wears a long black overcoat, a soot-black waistcoat with shiny brass buttons stretched over his belly and polished black shoes far too fine for gravel. Vain and silly rather than frightening.

Skredderlærlingen skredderlaerlingen · the Tailor's Apprentice

En tynn, ung skredderlærling med et strykejern under armen og ledningen surret rundt, som skal prøve å slippe inn i himmelen.

A thin, narrow-shouldered young man of about nineteen with a narrow pale face, a long pointed nose, big anxious grey eyes and neat, slicked-down black hair with a straight side parting. He wears a snug plum-purple knitted vest over a white shirt, slim grey trousers and black trainers, with a yellow tape measure round his neck and a red pincushion on his wrist, and carries an electric steam iron under his arm with its cord wrapped round it.

#05 · smeden, var-herre, sankt-peter
modern · after paragraph 33
Han trengte ikke lang betenkningstid. Han pekte ut vinduet, på det gamle pæretreet ved verkstedveggen. «Den jeg ber klatre opp i det pæretreet, skal bli sittende der til jeg selv sier at han kan komme ned.» Så nikket han mot pauserommet og den slitte lenestolen med gaffateip på armlenet. «Den jeg ber sette seg i den stolen, skal bli sittende til jeg selv sier at han kan reise seg.» Til slutt tok han opp ei lita veske av flettet ståltråd. Han hadde laget den i lærlingtida og brukte den fortsatt til mynter, som eneste mann i fylket. «Og den jeg ber krype inn i denne, skal bli der til jeg selv gir ham lov til å krype ut.»

Picture: Halvor, in his sooty grey hoodie, stands on a bare rocky hilltop at blue dusk, seen from behind in three-quarter view, his phone glowing blank in one hand. He gazes across ridge after ridge of dark spruce forest and deep-blue mountains to where, far, far away, the golden towers of Soria Moria glitter under a rising full moon, a place no map knows.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Halvor: A tall, lanky young man of about twenty with a lazy slouch, a long face, a long straight nose, sleepy, half-closed hazel eyes, a slow lopsided smile and messy auburn hair falling over his forehead, with soot on his hands and cheeks. He wears a soot-streaked grey hoodie with holes at the elbows, baggy faded black joggers and battered grey trainers.

Story world: Present-day Norway, and a strange, empty land beyond the sea that no map knows. Halvor's parents live in a small, old white wooden house on a hillside in a coastal village, below a big farm that rents out rooms, near a large lake. Across the sea lie fields and meadows without fences, power lines or signs, where three troll castles stand far apart, each finer than the last: the first of glass and steel, greenhouse-warm with palms; the second with a pool glowing turquoise; the third of black glass and dark stone. In each castle a huge troll sword set with gold and blue stones hangs on the wall beside a small brown flask of troll drink. The wishing ring is a smooth, lukewarm grey band like a smart ring. Soria Moria is a palace of golden towers far beyond forests and mountains.

This story's season, light and colours: Early autumn by the sea: long blue dusks and clear moonlit nights, the cool white glow of glass castles against indigo skies, a pool shining turquoise in the dusk and golden fairy lights at Soria Moria. Indoors: warm amber firelight in the little house. Daylight is pale and silvery, with accents of the youngest princess's red.

Art style: Contemporary Scandinavian editorial illustration: flat, graphic shapes with subtle risograph grain and a little hand-drawn texture, clean confident lines and a limited palette of spot inks led by deep petrol blue, with fjord teal, lingonberry red, honey mustard, sage green, warm paper off-white and ink charcoal, like the pages of a risograph-printed book, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, in the cool, clear Nordic light of today. Present-day Norway: fjord towns, suburbs, farms with tractors, cabins, ferries, roadside petrol stations, offices and flats, grey rain and bright snow, with people in modern clothes such as rain jackets, knitted sweaters, hoodies, suits and work wear. The magic of the tale appears plainly in this everyday world: trolls, talking animals and enchantments look real and slightly absurd, drawn in the same flat style. Every character has their own face, build, age, hair and clothes exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Dry humour, careful composition with one focal point and plenty of negative space. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles, logos, signs or readable screens. Phones and screens show only light or simple shapes.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Suitable for readers of all ages: no blood, wounds or gore, and no killing shown. Show danger and cruelty through atmosphere, posture and suspense, never through injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.

Characters

Halvor halvor · Halvor

En ung mann som har sittet foran peisen og raket i asken hele livet, men som hogger hodene av tre troll og går til verdens ende for å finne Siri igjen.

A tall, lanky young man of about twenty with a lazy slouch, a long face, a long straight nose, sleepy, half-closed hazel eyes, a slow lopsided smile and messy auburn hair falling over his forehead, with soot on his hands and cheeks. He wears a soot-streaked grey hoodie with holes at the elbows, baggy faded black joggers and battered grey trainers.

Halvor i dress halvor-suit · Halvor in the Suit

Halvor i dressen fra prinsessene, som sitter som om den var sydd til ham, og med ønskeringen fra Siri på fingeren.

A tall, lanky young man of about twenty with a long face, a long straight nose, sleepy hazel eyes, a slow lopsided smile and messy auburn hair falling over his forehead, washed clean and wearing a perfectly tailored royal-blue suit, a crisp white shirt open at the collar, a lingonberry-red pocket square and polished black leather shoes.

Den eldste prinsessa eldest-princess · the Eldest Princess

Den eldste av de tre prinsessene, som sitter ved rokken med tiara på hodet i det første slottet av glass og stål.

A tall, stately young woman of about twenty-four with warm golden-brown skin, a long oval face, a straight nose, calm dark-brown eyes, neat arched eyebrows and thick black hair coiled into two round buns over her ears. She wears a small silver tiara, a long pale-blue dress with long sleeves and a high neck, and white trainers peeking out under the hem.

Den mellomste prinsessa middle-princess · the Middle Princess

Den mellomste av de tre prinsessene, som har sittet så lenge i slottet med bassenget at mobilen hennes døde den første uka.

A short, lively young woman of about twenty-one with warm golden-brown skin, a round face with dimpled cheeks, a small button nose, merry black eyes and glossy black hair cut in a thick, chin-length bob with a straight fringe. She wears a small gold tiara, a sunflower-yellow satin dress with a white cardigan over it, a string of big white pearls and white sandals.

Siri av Soria Moria youngest-princess · the Youngest Princess

Den yngste av de tre prinsessene, som ser Halvor slåss mot trollet med ni hoder uten å skrike, og som gir ham en lunken ønskering med to regler.

A graceful, slender young woman of about twenty with warm golden-brown skin, a heart-shaped face, a small straight nose, large, bright dark-brown eyes with long lashes, a calm, watchful gaze and long, straight, glossy black hair falling loose to her waist. She wears a thin gold tiara, a long-sleeved red knitted dress to the ankles, black ankle boots and a tiny gold sun pendant on a fine chain.

Trollet med tre hoder three-headed-troll · the Three-Headed Troll

Trollet i det første slottet, som suser gjennom korridorene så glassveggene synger, og stikker alle tre hodene inn gjennom døra.

A big, pear-shaped troll about twice as tall as a man, with knobbly blue-grey skin like wet slate, long dangling arms and huge flat feet. He has exactly three heads side by side on his broad shoulders, each with a big round nose: the left head is sleepy, with droopy eyelids and a faded red beanie; the middle head is grumpy, with one bushy black eyebrow; the right head is surprised, with round eyes and a tuft of white hair. He wears a cracked brown leather jacket tied with rope.

Trollet med seks hoder six-headed-troll · the Six-Headed Troll

Trollet i slottet med bassenget, som er så stort og digert at det må gå sidelengs inn gjennom døra.

A huge, barrel-shaped troll about three times as tall as a man, with pale sandstone-yellow skin covered in brown freckles and warts, and shoulders so wide that he must turn sideways to get through doors. He has exactly six heads in one long row along his shoulders, each with a long pointed nose, small beady eyes and a stiff tuft of black hair. He wears a huge patchwork coat stitched together from old tarpaulins and sacks, and goes barefoot.

Trollet med ni hoder nine-headed-troll · the Nine-Headed Troll

Det største og seigeste av de tre trollene, som vrir seg sidelengs inn i slottet av svart glass så karmen knaker.

An enormous troll, the biggest of the three, about four times as tall as a man, with dark charcoal-grey skin, rough and lumpy like wet rock, a round belly and thick, stumpy legs. He has exactly nine small, round heads on short, thick necks, spread in a wide fan above his shoulders, each with a potato nose, bushy white eyebrows and a wide, frog-like mouth. He wears a ragged cloak of old sheepskins and a belt of knotted rope.

Mora mother · the Mother

Halvors mor, som tror at den fremmede i dress er fra kommunen, helt til skinnet fra peisen faller på ansiktet hans.

A small, sturdy, quick-moving woman of about sixty with a round chin, a wide mouth made for laughing, a little upturned nose, bright brown eyes and grey-streaked dark-brown hair tied up in a faded indigo scarf knotted on top of her head. She wears a heather-purple knitted jumper with rolled-up sleeves, a faded green apron, grey trousers and wooden clogs.

Faren father · the Father

Halvors far, en stille mann som har limt den beste stolen i huset tre ganger, og som bukker for den fremmede i dress.

A broad, slow-moving, heavy-set man of about sixty-five with a big round face, ruddy cheeks, a bulbous nose, a bushy salt-and-pepper beard and a bald head under a knitted blue beanie. He wears a worn moss-green fleece jacket over a checked flannel shirt, brown work trousers and heavy work boots.

Kjerringa med den lange nesa old-cottage-woman · the Old Woman

Ei eldgammel kone i ei skakk hytte dypt inne i skogen, som spør månen og Vestavinden om veien og bytter til seg hesten, for bussen til kirka er lagt ned.

A tall, bony, very old woman with a long thin neck, knobbly hands, a wrinkled, cheerful face, small twinkling black eyes and an enormously long, thin, pointed nose with a rosy tip, long enough to poke the embers with. Wisps of dove-grey hair peep out from under a white knitted hat. She wears a faded heather-blue fleece jumper, a long grey skirt, a black apron and green rubber boots.

Vestavinden west-wind · the West Wind

En travel vind som suser inn i hver krok av verden, er på vei til Soria Moria for å tørke tøy til bryllupet, og lar Halvor henge med så godt han kan.

A wild, friendly wind spirit the size of a big man, with a round, rosy, beardless face, a wide merry grin and bright green eyes. His long streaming hair is made of whirling leaves and spruce needles, with three bright plastic clothes-pegs clipped in it, and an orange hi-vis vest flaps around his chest. From the waist down his body turns into long, curling swirls of misty grey-green air full of spinning leaves.

Behind her, through an open ground-floor window, the polite bridegroom with the nice teeth is tumbling out backwards into a flower bed, still smiling politely. The guests stare.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Halvor in the Suit: A tall, lanky young man of about twenty with a long face, a long straight nose, sleepy hazel eyes, a slow lopsided smile and messy auburn hair falling over his forehead, washed clean and wearing a perfectly tailored royal-blue suit, a crisp white shirt open at the collar, a lingonberry-red pocket square and polished black leather shoes.
- the Youngest Princess: A graceful, slender young woman of about twenty with warm golden-brown skin, a heart-shaped face, a small straight nose, large, bright dark-brown eyes with long lashes, a calm, watchful gaze and long, straight, glossy black hair falling loose to her waist. She wears a thin gold tiara, a long-sleeved red knitted dress to the ankles, black ankle boots and a tiny gold sun pendant on a fine chain.

Story world: Present-day Norway, and a strange, empty land beyond the sea that no map knows. Halvor's parents live in a small, old white wooden house on a hillside in a coastal village, below a big farm that rents out rooms, near a large lake. Across the sea lie fields and meadows without fences, power lines or signs, where three troll castles stand far apart, each finer than the last: the first of glass and steel, greenhouse-warm with palms; the second with a pool glowing turquoise; the third of black glass and dark stone. In each castle a huge troll sword set with gold and blue stones hangs on the wall beside a small brown flask of troll drink. The wishing ring is a smooth, lukewarm grey band like a smart ring. Soria Moria is a palace of golden towers far beyond forests and mountains.

This story's season, light and colours: Early autumn by the sea: long blue dusks and clear moonlit nights, the cool white glow of glass castles against indigo skies, a pool shining turquoise in the dusk and golden fairy lights at Soria Moria. Indoors: warm amber firelight in the little house. Daylight is pale and silvery, with accents of the youngest princess's red.

- the Youngest Foal: A small, slender foal, the youngest and smallest of seven, with long, knobbly legs, a glossy light-chestnut coat, a short flaxen mane that stands up like a brush, a long flaxen tail, soft pointed ears, big dark eyes with a clever, far too human look and a neat white star on his forehead.

Story world: Present-day Norway at midsummer. Askeladden's family lives in a small, run-down house where the gravel road and the mobile coverage end, with a wood stove in the living room. Down in the valley lies the royal estate: a castle of grey stone and glass with guards at the gate, a courtyard the size of a football pitch and a long stable building with skylights and shiny steel stalls. The seven foals are glossy chestnut foals with flaxen manes and tails; the youngest, a lighter chestnut, has a white star on his forehead. The knitting woman sits on a low stone at a narrow cleft by a mountain path. A birch stump so big that three men could not reach around it hides steps down to a small earthen room. Beyond a long bridge that is on no map stands a small, black-tarred church with a tall tower.

Characters

Askeladden askeladden · Askeladden

Yngstesønnen som alle undervurderer, men som nekter å gi etter for lettvinte snarveier og følger sporene helt til han kan bryte trolldommen.

A sturdy, broad-shouldered young man of about nineteen with full, round, sun-browned cheeks, a short straight nose, calm green eyes, a steady, determined smile and thick sandy-brown hair tied back in a short ponytail. He wears a faded rust-orange hoodie, dark-green cargo trousers, sturdy black boots and a small brown canvas backpack.

Kongen kongen · the King

En streng, mistenksom hersker som setter brutale vilkår for å teste hvem som virkelig kan mestre de sju føllene og forstå hemmeligheten deres.

A lean, severe king of about sixty, tall and straight-backed, with a long, bony face, stern frown lines, sharp, narrow hazel eyes under bushy black eyebrows and a short, neatly trimmed grey beard. He wears a long dark charcoal overcoat over a dark-red roll-neck jumper, charcoal trousers, polished black shoes and a heavy gold signet ring.

Den gamle strikkekona den-gamle-strikkekona · the Knitting Woman

Ei krokrygget gammel kone ved bergsprekken som lokker med trøst og hvile for å få gjeterne til å svikte.

A tiny, hunched old woman no taller than a ten-year-old child, with a small, wrinkled face, a very long, pointed nose that nearly touches her chin, little twinkling black eyes, a sweet, sly smile and wisps of white hair. She wears many layered cardigans and scarves in faded blue, brown, plum and grey over a long dark skirt, fingerless mittens and worn felt boots, and she is always knitting something very long and grey.

Det yngste føllet det-yngste-follet · the Youngest Foal

Askeladdens nøkkelallierte blant de forheksede føllene, den som snakker og leder ham til sverdet, kirka og veien som kan gjøre dem til prinser igjen.

A small, slender foal, the youngest and smallest of seven, with long, knobbly legs, a glossy light-chestnut coat, a short flaxen mane that stands up like a brush, a long flaxen tail, soft pointed ears, big dark eyes with a clever, far too human look and a neat white star on his forehead.

Den yngste prinsen den-yngste-prinsen · the Youngest Prince

Det yngste føllet slik han egentlig er: den yngste av de sju prinsene og lillebror til prinsessa, som gnir seg i nakken når trolldommen slipper.

A slim young man of about seventeen, the youngest of seven brothers, with a round, freckled face, big dark eyes, a huge beaming smile and tousled strawberry-blonde hair. He wears shining white clothes with gold trim: a white shirt embroidered with gold, with a small white star on the chest, a short white jacket, white trousers and white leather boots.

Prinsessa prinsessa · the Princess

Kongens datter, som nekter å bli gitt bort som premie, men gjerne blir sittende og snakke med Askeladden til sola står opp.

A cheerful young woman of about twenty with a round, freckled face, warm brown eyes, a wide, amused smile and a mass of bouncy strawberry-blonde curls falling past her shoulders. She wears a pale-green shirt dress with a white collar, a cropped denim jacket, white trainers and small gold earrings, each set with one green stone.

Den eldste broren eldste-bror · the Eldest Brother

Askeladdens storebror, som trodde at det med de røde remmene var et uttrykk, og som sover bort hele dagen med hodet i fanget til strikkekona.

A tall, gawky young man of about twenty-two with a long, bony face, a big chin, heavy-lidded eyes, a long nose, a lazy, lopsided grin and thick, wavy dark-blond hair that sticks up at the back. He wears a red-and-white checked flannel shirt with rolled sleeves, baggy brown work trousers held up by a single braces strap, a wide, frayed straw hat and scuffed white trainers.

De tre prinsessene i Hvittenland tentland · 16/16 pictures

Båten gikk hele natten.

Alt: En liten, hvit fiskebåt glir av seg selv over et mørkt hav om natten. Gutten sitter i båten i redningsvest, og langt fremme lyser en kritthvit strand.

At night on a vast, dark sea, the small white fishing boat glides along all by itself with a white wave at the bow and its engine silent. The Fisher Lad sits in it in an orange life jacket, his phone gone dark in his hand, looking up at the stars in wonder; far ahead, a thin line of dazzling white shore glows on the horizon under the first pale light of dawn.
